wat-pho.name: Wat Pho
wat-pho.type: A royal temple known for its Reclining Buddha and traditional medicine
wat-pho.title: Wat Pho in Bangkok: Reclining Buddha, Temple Grounds and Visitor Guide | ThaiLiveNow
wat-pho.description: Wat Pho, just south of Bangkok’s Grand Palace, is home to a 46-metre-long Reclining Buddha with mother-of-pearl inlay on its feet. Visit the Buddha hall, then explore the temple’s chedis, halls and other details across the grounds.
intro: Up close, the Reclining Buddha’s 46-metre golden body fills the hall. Look down at its feet to see 108 mother-of-pearl designs, where the statue’s immense scale meets fine craftsmanship. Wat Pho is a royal temple just south of Bangkok’s Grand Palace.

After seeing the Reclining Buddha, walk among the four royal chedis, each decorated in a different colour, and through galleries lined with Buddha images. Chinese-style stone figures and stone inscriptions on medicine and language also show how Wat Pho shared knowledge. You can also have a traditional massage after your visit for an additional fee.

experiences.title: The designs on the Reclining Buddha’s feet
paragraphs: Built during the reign of Rama III, the Reclining Buddha measures 46 metres long and 15 metres high. Take your time following the figure from its face along its outstretched body to its feet. The soles bear 108 mother-of-pearl designs made from shaped shell, bringing delicate craftsmanship to this monumental statue.

After taking in the golden figure, look closely at the mother-of-pearl on its soles. Small designs reflecting Buddhist cosmology form a closely arranged pattern. The Reclining Buddha is enshrined inside a hall, so enter the designated viewing area to see the statue and its decorated feet.

experiences.title: Four royal chedis in different colours
paragraphs: The four large chedis inside the white walls are associated with Kings Rama I through Rama IV. Green, white, yellow and deep blue mosaics give each tower a distinct look. Follow the colours to tell apart chedis that may seem similar at first.

The green chedi houses a damaged Phra Si Sanphet Buddha image brought from the royal palace in Ayutthaya. After Ayutthaya fell, the surviving image was moved to Bangkok and enshrined inside this chedi. A Buddha image from Ayutthaya’s former royal temple remains at Wat Pho today.

experiences.title: Galleries of Buddha images and Chinese-style stone figures
paragraphs: The temple describes the inner gallery of the double corridor around the main hall as holding about 150 Buddha images, with more than 244 in the outer gallery. These images were brought from northern Thailand during the reign of Rama I and are now covered in gold leaf. As you walk through the galleries, compare the faces and poses of the different images.

One hundred stone slabs inscribed with Thai verse from the reign of Rama III hang from the gallery pillars. This was a place to read and learn as well as to view Buddha images. Even if you do not read Thai, you can still take in the arrangement of the images beside the inscriptions.

Some Chinese-style stone figures along the paths came from stone ballast once carried on Chinese trading ships. You will see not only armed guardians, but also officials holding books, monks and working people. Look at their materials and depictions of people alongside the golden Buddha images.

experiences.title: Knowledge inscribed at the temple and traditional massage
paragraphs: Rama III had knowledge from several fields inscribed around the temple so people could learn from it. This is why Wat Pho is often likened to Thailand’s first university. The temple served not only as a place of worship, but also as a centre for sharing knowledge about subjects such as medicine and language.

Traditional massage is available, but **massage is not included in the temple admission ticket.** If you would like one after your visit, choose a service and pay separately. It can be a restful way to end a visit after exploring the halls and galleries.

rules.title: Arrive before last admission
paragraphs: The temple closes at 20:00, but **new visitors are admitted only until 19:30**. If you are visiting in the evening, do not plan your arrival around closing time.

rules.title: Massage is separate from temple admission
paragraphs: The massage pavilion accepts visitors **in person without advance reservations**. If you would like a massage after your visit, plan your route so you arrive **before the 18:00 registration cutoff**. Massage fees are not included in the temple admission ticket.

rules.title: Women cannot enter in shorts above the knee
paragraphs: Wat Pho **restricts women from entering in shorts that end above the knee**. Visitors of all genders are advised to cover their shoulders and knees. Wear a top with sleeves and long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees.

rules.title: Remove your shoes before entering worship halls
paragraphs: Before entering a religious building, **remove your shoes and place them on the designated rack.** Check the signs and shoe racks at the entrances to shrines and halls, and follow posted directions elsewhere on the grounds.

rules.title: Some areas for monks’ ceremonies are restricted
paragraphs: **Women may not enter areas specifically set aside for monks to perform ceremonies.** This does not restrict women from visiting the temple as a whole. Follow area-specific signs and staff directions around the grounds.

accessSections.title: Arrive by MRT or from a pier
paragraphs: From **Sanam Chai Station on the MRT Blue Line**, it is about a five-minute walk to the temple. If you are travelling by boat, you can reach the temple from Tha Tien Pier.

faq: Is a massage included in the Wat Pho admission ticket?
No. Temple admission and massage are charged separately. After visiting the Reclining Buddha and the temple grounds, you can choose a massage type and duration on site and pay the fee separately.
What can I see besides the Reclining Buddha?

After seeing the 108 mother-of-pearl designs on the 46-metre Reclining Buddha’s feet, walk among the four royal chedis associated with Rama I through Rama IV and through the galleries lined with Buddha images. You can also see Chinese-style stone figures and stone inscriptions about knowledge.
Can I get a massage if I visit in the evening?

New admission to the temple closes at 19:30, but the massage pavilion’s walk-in registration closes at 18:00. If you would like a massage after your visit, go to the pavilion before registration closes.
Which areas of Wat Pho are women not allowed to enter?

The restriction on women applies to designated areas set aside for monks’ ceremonies; it does not mean women cannot visit the temple as a whole. Remove your shoes before entering religious buildings and follow the signs for each area.

wat-arun.name: Wat Arun
wat-arun.thai: วัดอรุณราชวรารามราชวรมหาวิหาร
wat-arun.title: Wat Arun Bangkok: Temple, Riverside Views and Visitor Guide | ThaiLiveNow
wat-arun.description: Wat Arun, also called the Temple of Dawn, stands on the west bank of Bangkok’s Chao Phraya River. Admire its tall prang from the river, then look closely at the ceramic fragments and decorative details across the temple grounds.
intro: When the bright prang comes into view from a boat crossing the Chao Phraya River, you are nearing Wat Arun. Known as the Temple of Dawn, it stands on the west side of Bangkok. From the riverbank you can take in the tower’s outline; once inside the grounds, you can see ceramic fragments and small figures that are hard to make out from a distance.

After looking around the smaller towers surrounding the central prang and the guardians at the entrance, visit the Buddha image and murals inside the main hall. If you are crossing by boat from Wat Pho, you can see the full tower from the river and then examine its ceramic details and sculptures up close.

experiences.title: Look closely at the ceramic fragments on the central prang
paragraphs: The tall tower at the heart of Wat Arun is called the Phra Prang. From across the river, its height and long outline stand out first. Up close, you can see the ceramic fragments covering its surface and the decorations arranged like flowers. Take a closer look at the small pieces that make up its bright exterior.

Four smaller prangs stand around the central tower. Rather than photographing only the main tower and leaving, take a moment to notice the decorations and rooflines between the smaller ones too. Some stairs on the prangs are high and steep, so **use only the sections open to visitors on site.**

experiences.title: The name “Temple of Dawn” and its history
paragraphs: The temple’s name comes from Aruna, a Hindu deity associated with dawn. The site dates back to the Ayutthaya period, while the halls and towers you see today reflect later additions and restoration by successive dynasties. Wat Arun is more than a riverside viewpoint; religious activities have taken place here for a long time.

The Emerald Buddha was once enshrined at Wat Arun. After the dynasty changed, it was moved across the river to Wat Phra Kaew in Bangkok. From Wat Arun, look across the river towards the palace, where the statue is now kept, and you can see the distance between its former and present homes.

experiences.title: Guardian figures and the Buddha image and murals in the ordination hall
paragraphs: Two yaksha guardian figures stand at the temple entrance. They are larger than the small decorations on the prangs, so take a look at the figures guarding the entrance before walking straight towards the towers.

The ordination hall, called the ubosot, contains a Buddha image and murals. After seeing the ceramic decorations on the outer towers, step inside to look at the paintings too. **Remove your shoes before entering the hall** and look around quietly without blocking people who are praying.

experiences.title: Riverside views on the way by boat
paragraphs: You can cross the river from Tha Tien Pier on the Wat Pho side, or take a boat service that stops at Wat Arun Pier. From the boat, you can see the riverside temples and towers together; once you arrive, walk closer to the prang to examine its decorations. The boat fare and temple admission are charged separately.

experiences.title: The prang and its evening lights from the park across the river
paragraphs: Nagaraphirom Park is a public riverside park opposite Wat Arun. It offers a place to look across the river at the full outline of the prang without paying for a restaurant or rooftop seat. You can see the ceramic details inside the temple grounds, then come here to take in the river and tower together. Check whether the park is open before you visit and follow the on-site entry guidance.

The Tourism Authority of Thailand’s **2024 night-viewing guide** lists the main prang’s lights as running from **18:00 to 06:00 the following day.** This may vary with conditions on site. In daylight, the ceramic details stand out on the bright tower; after the lights come on, its outline rises above the dark river. These hours refer to the exterior lighting, **not the opening hours for entering the temple grounds.**

rules.title: Watch your step on the prang stairs
paragraphs: Some of the prang stairs are high, steep or narrow. **Use only the sections open to visitors on site**, and do not climb on or damage the decorations.

rules.title: What to wear when visiting the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear **clothing that covers the shoulders and knees.** A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a practical choice. Please visit in respectful clothing rather than a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

rules.title: Remove your shoes before entering the ordination hall
paragraphs: Please **remove your shoes** before entering the ordination hall (ubosot). If you use a wheelchair or pushchair, contact the temple office in advance to ask which entrance and viewing areas you can use.

accessSections.title: Walk from Itsaraphap Station
paragraphs: **Itsaraphap Station on the MRT Blue Line** is on the same west bank of the Chao Phraya River as Wat Arun. From this station, you can walk to the temple without taking a boat across the river.

accessSections.title: Wat Arun Pier or the Tha Tien cross-river ferry
paragraphs: At Sathorn Pier, choose a route that stops at Wat Arun Pier. The stop lists differ between regular express boats and tourist boats.

From Tha Tien Pier on the Wat Pho side, you can take the cross-river ferry. This is a different service from boats travelling along the river, so when buying your ticket, ask for **the boat crossing to Wat Arun.**

faq: How much is admission?
Admission is 200 baht for foreign visitors and free for Thai visitors. This is the temple entry fee; the boat fare for crossing the river is separate.
What are the opening hours?
The temple is open daily from 08:00 to 18:00. If you visit in the late afternoon, leave enough time to explore before closing.
What should I wear?
Visitors of all genders are advised to wear modest clothing that covers the shoulders and knees. Remove your shoes before entering the ordination hall.
How do I get there?

You can walk from Itsaraphap Station on the MRT Blue Line. If travelling by boat, choose a service that stops at Wat Arun Pier. If you are already on the Wat Pho side, you can also take the cross-river ferry from Tha Tien Pier.
Can I see the temple from outside without going in?

Yes. You can view the tower from the riverbank across the river. You need an admission ticket to explore the temple grounds. Follow the on-site guidance about which parts of the tower are open to visitors.
Are Wat Arun and Wat Pho the same place?

No. They are separate temples on opposite sides of the Chao Phraya River. Wat Arun, on the west bank, is known for its prang; Wat Pho, on the east bank, is known for the Reclining Buddha. Each requires its own admission ticket.
Can I see the prang after sunset?

Entry to the temple grounds closes at 18:00. You can see the exterior of the prang from across the river, and the Tourism Authority of Thailand’s 2024 night-viewing guide lists the main prang’s lights as running from 18:00 to 06:00 the following day. The lighting hours are not the temple’s opening hours.

wat-phra-kaew.name: Wat Phra Kaew
wat-phra-kaew.thai: วัดพระศรีรัตนศาสดาราม
wat-phra-kaew.type: Royal temple within the Grand Palace complex
wat-phra-kaew.title: Wat Phra Kaew: Emerald Buddha and Grand Palace Visitor Guide | ThaiLiveNow
wat-phra-kaew.description: Wat Phra Kaew, inside Bangkok’s Grand Palace, is the royal temple that enshrines the Emerald Buddha. Explore the temple halls and palace architecture with one ticket; you do not need to find it as a separate temple or buy a second ticket.
intro: Wat Phra Kaew is the royal temple inside Bangkok’s Grand Palace where the Emerald Buddha is enshrined. The grounds bring together sights of very different scale and style, from the small image on its high altar to golden chedis, monumental guardians and gallery murals that tell a connected story.

Admission to Wat Phra Kaew is included with the Grand Palace ticket, so you do not need a separate temple ticket. Along with the Emerald Buddha, explore the Ramakien murals in the galleries and the decoration outside the halls for a closer look at Thai royal art and Buddhist architecture.
facts: **500 baht for international visitors** · Includes Wat Phra Kaew and the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles
Available from one month before your visit

experiences.title: The Emerald Buddha on a high altar
paragraphs: The Emerald Buddha sits in a meditative pose high on a golden wooden altar. The Grand Palace lists its height as 66 cm, including its base. It is small compared with the surrounding buildings, yet it is one of Thailand’s most deeply revered images.

The image has three sets of seasonal garments for the hot, rainy and cool seasons. On appointed lunar-calendar dates, the King performs a ceremony to change the garments. Made with gold and jewels, the robes also show the changing work of royal artisans through the seasons.

experiences.title: The Ramakien story across the gallery
paragraphs: The galleries surrounding the temple buildings show 178 scenes from the Ramakien, Thailand’s national epic. The story of Prince Rama rescuing Sida unfolds through scenes of gods, people, monkeys and giants, with palaces and forests along the way.

The murals show more than grand battles: everyday life inside and outside the palace appears alongside animals. Even if you do not know the full story, take time to look at the figures’ poses and clothing, and the buildings and forests. It is a rewarding stop for anyone travelling with an interest in art.

experiences.title: Six pairs of giants and a golden chedi
paragraphs: The giant guardians at the doors represent characters from the Ramakien. Six pairs face the main hall as a sign of reverence toward the Emerald Buddha, according to the Grand Palace. Compare their different colours, faces and headdresses.

The bell-shaped Phra Si Rattana Chedi was built during the reign of Rama IV to enshrine a Buddha relic. It was originally white, then covered in gold-coloured mosaics imported from Italy during the reign of Rama V. Look closely at the mosaic surface as you walk around the chedi.

experiences.title: Visit the temple as part of a Grand Palace itinerary
paragraphs: The 500-baht Grand Palace ticket for international visitors includes Wat Phra Kaew and the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles. You can continue from the temple to the palace buildings and textile museum, but admission does not grant unrestricted access to the interior of every building.

Royal ceremonies and worship still take place here. **Dress according to the Grand Palace clothing rules**, and follow on-site instructions in areas restricted for events or other reasons. To avoid confusion with temples of the same name elsewhere, navigate to Wat Phra Kaew inside Bangkok’s Grand Palace.

rules.title: Sleeveless tops and short bottoms are not allowed
paragraphs: Entry is restricted for clothing such as **sleeveless tops, short tops, see-through clothing, shorts and miniskirts**. Torn or tight-fitting trousers and pyjamas are also prohibited. Wear long bottoms and a top that covers your shoulders.

rules.title: Online tickets cannot be changed or refunded
paragraphs: **Online tickets cannot be refunded or changed to another date or time.** Buy after your travel plans are set, and double-check your visit date before paying.

rules.title: Visitor entrance and day-of restrictions
paragraphs: Since 2024, the operator has listed **Mani Noppharat Gate** as the visitor entrance. On days with royal events or temporary restrictions, follow the entrance instructions for that day. Drone flights over the Grand Palace are prohibited.

rules.title: Recommended clothing for visiting the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear **clothing that covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a practical choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

rules.title: Audio guides are rented separately
paragraphs: A personal audio guide is available to rent for **200 baht**, separately from the Grand Palace ticket. It is offered in eight languages: English, French, German, Japanese, Mandarin Chinese, Russian, Spanish and Thai; Korean is not available. You must leave a passport or an Amex, Mastercard or Visa credit card as a deposit. Ask the rental desk about availability and deposit requirements on the day.

accessSections.title: Finding the Grand Palace entrance
paragraphs: Wat Phra Kaew is **inside the Grand Palace complex in Bangkok**, so enter through the visitor entrance for the palace. Tha Chang Pier is listed as a boat access point. There is no separate entrance just for the temple; visitors enter as part of the Grand Palace visit.

faq: Do I need to buy a separate ticket for Wat Phra Kaew?
No. Wat Phra Kaew is included in the 500-baht Grand Palace ticket for foreign visitors. The ticket also includes the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles.
What can I see besides the Emerald Buddha?

You can see the gallery murals depicting the Ramakien in 178 scenes, six pairs of giant guardian figures facing the main hall, and the gold-mosaic-covered Phra Si Rattana Chedi. The Emerald Buddha is on a high altar, so take in the small details you can see from below as well as the larger buildings around the grounds.
Is an English-language audio guide available?

Yes. The Grand Palace’s personal audio guide is available in English, French, German, Spanish, Russian, Japanese, Mandarin Chinese and Thai, but not Korean. Rental costs 200 baht. You must leave your passport or one of the listed types of credit card as a deposit.

wat-saket.name: Wat Saket and the Golden Mount
wat-saket.english: Wat Saket and the Golden Mount
wat-saket.type: Golden Mount chedi and old-city viewpoint temple
wat-saket.title: Wat Saket and the Golden Mount: Bangkok Temple and Viewpoint | ThaiLiveNow
wat-saket.description: Wat Saket is known for the Golden Mount in Bangkok’s old city. Climb the steps up the man-made hill to the golden chedi and look out over the low rooftops and city streets.
intro: Above the rooftops of Bangkok’s Old Town, a golden chedi marks the Golden Mount at Wat Saket. Climb the stairs up the man-made hill and you will see worshippers near the chedi as well as the city spread around it.

Look around the lower part of the temple, then climb the stairs to the golden reliquary chedi and views over the Old Town. Reaching the top and returning means using the stairs, so this visit suits companions who can manage them and have time to explore at an easy pace.

experiences.title: A golden mount built above an old temple
paragraphs: The Golden Mount is a man-made hill built at the temple, not a natural mountain. Its Thai name, Phu Khao Thong, means “Golden Mountain”. Completed during the reign of Rama V, the hill rises about 77 metres above the temple roofs, making it easy to spot as you walk through the Old Town.

From a distance, the hill and golden chedi form a single outline. At its base, you can make out the temple buildings and the stairs leading upwards. Before climbing, take in the whole site from below. You can see the older temple, which dates back to the Ayutthaya period, and the man-made hill added later.

experiences.title: Rama I’s ceremony remembered in the temple’s name
paragraphs: Wat Saket existed before the Golden Mount was built. It was called Wat Sakae during the Ayutthaya period and received its present name in 1782, when the Bangkok dynasty began. Knowing this history helps show that the golden chedi at the summit is only part of the site’s story.

The Tourism Authority also recounts that Rama I stayed here to have his head shaved before his coronation ceremony. “Saket” is a royal term associated with the king’s hair grooming. As you think about the name left by this royal ceremony, start by looking around the old temple at the foot of the hill.

experiences.title: The reliquary chedi after 344 steps
paragraphs: There are 344 steps winding up the Golden Mount. Reaching the chedi you see from below means climbing them, so consider first whether you are comfortable with the stairs. The golden chedi at the top enshrines relics, making this both a viewpoint and a place of worship.

From the upper gallery, you can turn in different directions to see Bangkok’s Old Town. Rather than looking in one direction and heading straight back down, walk around the chedi and follow the rooftops and streets as they meet the horizon. Step aside where worshippers are gathering so you do not block their way.

rules.title: Plan for the steps before you set out
paragraphs: Visiting the Golden Mount means **climbing the steps and walking back down again**. Allow enough time for the round trip as well as your time at the viewpoint.

rules.title: Recommended clothing for visiting the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear **clothing that covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a practical choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

accessSections.title: Get there from Sam Yot MRT Station
paragraphs: The Golden Mount is listed as about a 15-minute walk from **Sam Yot Station on the MRT Blue Line**. Search for Wat Saket or Golden Mount as your destination.

faq: Is the Golden Mount a natural mountain?
No. It is a man-made hill, about 77 metres high, added above the old Wat Saket temple. You can view the temple and hill together from below, then climb to the golden reliquary chedi at the summit.
Do I need to climb to the summit to see the temple?

You can see the temple at the foot of the hill, but you need to climb the stairs to reach the worship area beside the golden reliquary chedi and the Old Town views. Visiting the summit means climbing up and back down.

wat-phra-that-doi-suthep.thai: วัดพระธาตุดอยสุเทพ
wat-phra-that-doi-suthep.type: Mountain temple and Chiang Mai viewpoint
wat-phra-that-doi-suthep.title: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep: Chiang Mai Temple and Viewpoint | ThaiLiveNow
wat-phra-that-doi-suthep.description: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep sits on Doi Suthep mountain west of Chiang Mai. Visit the golden chedi, climb the naga-lined staircase and look out over the city from the terrace.
intro: After following the mountain road west of Chiang Mai, you reach Doi Suthep Temple and its long staircase guarded by naga figures. From the terrace above, the city spreads out below, bringing together a northern Thai place of worship and a sweeping urban view.

Inside the temple, you can see worshippers circling the golden chedi and details in the Lanna style. It also makes a rewarding stop after visiting temples in the Old City if you would like to look back over Chiang Mai from the mountain. If you take the paid cable car instead of the stairs, plan around its operating hours, which differ from the temple’s opening hours. Allow time for the mountain drive so you can take in the chedi and city views at an easy pace.

experiences.title: Pay your respects at the golden chedi
paragraphs: At the heart of this hilltop temple stands a golden chedi about 22 metres tall. It is said to enshrine a Buddha relic and is the spiritual centre of the temple founded by King Kuena, who ruled the north. Set aside time both to pay your respects at the chedi and to enjoy the city view from the terrace.

The tourism authority describes a devotional practice of carrying lotus flowers and incense, walking clockwise around the chedi three times, praying and making an offering. It says sets of lotus flowers and incense are sold at the temple entrance. If you wish to take part, follow the on-site instructions and route, and leave space for worshippers as you watch.

experiences.title: Climb the naga steps or take the cable car
paragraphs: A pair of naga sculptures runs alongside the 306 steps leading up to the temple. From below, their bodies appear to stretch all the way up the staircase. Walk up if you want to see the steps and their decoration along the way.
If someone in your group would find the climb difficult, the cable car is another option. **It operates approximately 06:00–18:00**, so plan to arrive within those hours if you intend to use it.

experiences.title: Look out over Chiang Mai from the terrace
paragraphs: After exploring the worship area around the golden chedi, head to the terrace facing the city. Chiang Mai spreads out below the mountain, offering a different perspective from walking among the temples in the old city.

The temple is reached by a mountain road from town. Decide whether to climb the steps or take the cable car, and leave time for the terrace. Even if the view is your main reason for visiting, move quietly through the temple and give worshippers room.

rules.title: The cable car closes before the temple
paragraphs: The temple is open into the evening, but **the cable car operates only until approximately 18:00**. If you plan to ride it, do not plan your visit around the temple’s later closing time.

rules.title: What to wear at the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear clothing that **covers the shoulders and knees**. A top with sleeves and long trousers or a skirt covering the knees are suitable choices. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

accessSections.title: Reach the hilltop temple west of Chiang Mai
paragraphs: The temple sits on Doi Suthep mountain, west of Chiang Mai, and you need to travel up the mountain road to reach it. Set your destination to **Wat Phra That Doi Suthep**, rather than the wider Doi Suthep area. From the arrival point, reach the temple grounds by climbing the 306 naga steps or taking the paid cable car.

faq: Can I reach the temple without climbing the naga steps?

Yes. You can take the paid cable car instead of climbing the 306 naga steps. It is listed as operating approximately 06:00–18:00, closing before the temple itself. Walk up if you want to see the naga decorations along the staircase.
What can I see at Doi Suthep besides the view?

The temple’s centrepiece is a golden chedi about 22 metres tall, with Lanna decoration and worshippers walking clockwise around it. After seeing the chedi, go to the terrace overlooking the city to experience both the worship area and the mountain view.

wat-phra-singh.name: Wat Phra Singh
wat-phra-singh.thai: วัดพระสิงห์
wat-phra-singh.type: Old City temple with Lanna Buddha image and murals
wat-phra-singh.title: Wat Phra Singh: Lanna Art and Buddha Image in Chiang Mai | ThaiLiveNow
wat-phra-singh.description: Wat Phra Singh is a Chiang Mai Old City temple with Lanna-style halls, murals and the Phra Singh Buddha image. Look beyond the golden chedi to see the carved wood and paintings inside Viharn Lai Kham.
intro: At Wat Phra Singh in Chiang Mai’s Old City, you can see a golden chedi and the Lai Kham Viharn, which houses the Phra Singh Buddha image. Murals on the two side walls depict the stories of Suwannahong and the Golden Conch, as well as clothing and details of everyday life from the period.

The temple dates to 1345, while the murals are thought to have been painted around the viharn’s renovation in 1863. After paying respects to the Buddha image, compare the scenes on both side walls, then step outside to see the golden chedi.
facts: 50 baht · Check on site which halls are covered by the ticket

experiences.title: The Phra Singh Buddha and story murals in Lai Kham Viharn
paragraphs: Inside the grounds, Lai Kham Viharn houses the Phra Singh Buddha, also known as Phra Phuttha Sihing. After paying your respects, look at the walls: the north side tells the story of Suwannahong and the south side the Golden Conch. The rear wall depicts Buddhas of the past.

The paintings go beyond Buddhist themes. They also show clothing, architecture and everyday life at the time, so even visitors unfamiliar with the stories can take their time looking at the figures and street scenes. Please avoid blocking the way for people who are worshipping.

experiences.title: A temple founded in 1345 and murals from a later period
paragraphs: Wat Phra Singh was founded in 1345 by King Pha Yu of the Lanna Kingdom. It was first called Wat Li Chiang Phra; it became known by its present name after King Saen Mueang Ma brought the Phra Singh Buddha image from Chiang Rai. The approximately 50-metre golden chedi and the viharn housing the image show how the royal temple and its object of worship are connected.

The murals in Lai Kham Viharn are thought to have been painted during renovations in 1863. The Suwannahong and Golden Conch stories are attributed to different painters. Compare how the figures and scenes are depicted on the two walls of the same viharn.

experiences.title: The Phra Singh Buddha procession during Songkran
paragraphs: During Songkran, a tradition carries the Phra Singh Buddha on a special platform through Chiang Mai. The image usually worshipped inside the viharn is brought out into the city for the New Year festival. The tourism authority describes events between 13 and 15 April, but check the announcement for the year you plan to visit for the actual procession details.

Outside the festival period, visit Lai Kham Viharn to see the Buddha image and murals, then explore the golden chedi outside. Keeping the regular worship space and the festival procession distinct helps you know what to expect on different dates.

rules.title: Recommended clothing for visiting the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear **clothing that covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a practical choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

accessSections.title: Find the temple in the Old City
paragraphs: The destination is **Wat Phra Singh on Sam Lan Road, at number 2**. Search for Chiang Mai as well to avoid confusing it with temples of the same name elsewhere.

faq: What can I see inside Lai Kham Viharn?

The viharn houses the Phra Singh Buddha, also known as Phra Phuttha Sihing. Murals on the north wall depict Suwannahong and those on the south wall the Golden Conch; they also show clothing and details of everyday life at the time.
Can I see the Phra Singh Buddha outside Songkran?

You can usually pay your respects to the Buddha image and see the murals inside Lai Kham Viharn. The procession that carries the image through the city is a separate Songkran tradition. The tourism authority describes events on 13–15 April, but the procession schedule for a particular year may vary with the announcement.

wat-chedi-luang.name: Wat Chedi Luang
wat-chedi-luang.thai: วัดเจดีย์หลวง
wat-chedi-luang.type: Old City temple with a large brick chedi
wat-chedi-luang.title: Wat Chedi Luang: Brick Chedi and Lanna Temple in Chiang Mai | ThaiLiveNow
wat-chedi-luang.description: Wat Chedi Luang is a Chiang Mai Old City temple with a large brick chedi at its centre. See its broken summit, naga sculptures and surrounding halls in the Lanna style.
intro: You have reached Wat Chedi Luang when you come upon the large brick chedi with its broken summit in the middle of Chiang Mai’s Old City. Its broad base and naga sculptures along the stairs give a sense of the scale of this old structure, quite different from a gleaming golden tower.

This temple brings together a large chedi holding the history of the Lanna Kingdom and halls that are still in use. First look at the chedi from a little distance, then go closer to see its base and details. Continue to the Lanna-style halls still used today to see how historic architecture and active places of worship share the same grounds.

experiences.title: Mount Meru at the heart of old Chiang Mai
paragraphs: Wat Chedi Luang is said to have been begun in 1391 by King Saen Mueang Ma in memory of his late father. “Luang” means “large” in the northern dialect. The name points to a large chedi, but it is also interesting to consider why the tower stands at the heart of the city.

The Tourism Authority explains that kings of the time believed the dynasty would prosper if they built a large tower at the centre of the city, modelled on Mount Meru at the centre of the Buddhist universe, with temples in the eight directions. From in front of the broad base, you can think about the centre of the old city as well as the brick ruin itself.

experiences.title: A collapsed summit and restored brick structure
paragraphs: The upper part of the chedi was damaged in an earthquake in 1545 and later repaired, according to the historical account. Rather than having a complete spire rebuilt, the site lets you imagine the tower’s former scale from the bricks that remain.

From a distance, you can see the outline with its broken upper section; up close, the layered base and brick surface stand out. If you want to take in the surviving architecture, look at it from more than one side instead of photographing it from a single spot.

experiences.title: Five-headed naga and a Lanna hall
paragraphs: Eight sculptures of five-headed naga line the base and stairs of the large chedi. After looking up at the collapsed top, turn your attention to the lower part: the surviving sculptures give a sense of the tower’s original scale and decoration.

The Lanna-style main hall in the grounds has a different roofline and materials from the brick tower. Seeing a tower whose summit was damaged in an earthquake alongside a worship space still in use is one of the site’s distinctive features. Follow on-site instructions about which halls are open to visitors.

rules.title: Recommended clothing for visiting the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear **clothing that covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a practical choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

accessSections.title: Find it in the centre of the Old City
paragraphs: The address is **103 Phra Pokklao Road** in the centre of Chiang Mai’s Old City. Set Wat Chedi Luang, with its large surviving brick chedi, as your destination.

faq: Why is the top of the chedi broken off?

The upper part of the large brick chedi was damaged in the 1545 earthquake and later repaired, leaving the outline you see today. Its broad base and surviving layers of brick give a sense of how large the tower once was.
What can I see besides the chedi?

You can see eight five-headed naga sculptures on the base and stairs, as well as a Lanna-style hall still used as a place of worship. Compare the collapsed ruin with the temple building still in use within the same grounds.

wat-rong-khun.name: Wat Rong Khun
wat-rong-khun.thai: วัดร่องขุ่น
wat-rong-khun.type: Contemporary Buddhist art temple known as the White Temple
wat-rong-khun.title: Wat Rong Khun (White Temple): Art and Visitor Guide | ThaiLiveNow
wat-rong-khun.description: Wat Rong Khun, the White Temple in Chiang Rai, is designed by local artist Chalermchai Kositpipat around Buddhist and mythological themes. Unlike an old brick ruin, it presents contemporary Buddhist art through white architecture and sculpture.
intro: Wat Rong Khun in Chiang Rai is known as the White Temple for its white architecture and fine, pointed sculptures that tell Buddhist stories. Conceived by Chiang Rai artist Chalermchai Kositpipat, it invites you to look at the bridge before the white hall and figures drawn from mythology as you would look at an artwork.

The White Temple is about 14 km from central Chiang Rai, so allow time to travel there and back. If you enjoy contemporary Thai art or architecture, take your time with the white hall, bridge and sculptures depicting mythological beings. Look at the overall form of the buildings as well as the fine details up close.

experiences.title: A white temple created by Chalermchai Kositpipat
paragraphs: Wat Rong Khun is a contemporary temple created to express an artist’s ideas, rather than a restoration of an old building. Chalermchai Kositpipat expressed Buddhist and mythological themes through white halls and sculptures. Details running along the roof edges and around the windows make the whole building feel like one work of art.

experiences.title: A story of hell and heaven along the bridge
paragraphs: The bridge leading to the white main hall represents a Buddhist journey from hell towards heaven. The Tourism Authority describes the bridge and sculptures around the hall as parts of one journey. First take in the whole white building from a distance; as you approach the bridge, you will see how the sculptures on both sides lead towards the main hall.

As you cross the bridge and approach the hall, the white decorations that looked like one surface from afar resolve into smaller sculptures along the roof edges and windows. Follow the route open to visitors on site, and view the decorations and main hall from areas where access is permitted.

experiences.title: A contrast between white halls and golden architecture
paragraphs: The grounds also have a restroom building with a golden exterior that contrasts with the white halls. Its detailed decoration shows the artist’s different expressions across the buildings, including an everyday facility. Follow the on-site guidance about the artworks and areas open to visitors indoors.

If you also visit the Blue Temple in Chiang Rai, you can compare the white halls here with the blue halls there. They are separate locations and require separate journeys, but it is easy to remember the contrast between the white sculptures at one and the blue and gold decorations at the other.

rules.title: Follow on-site photography instructions for each area
paragraphs: Taking photos of the exterior is different from photographing works inside the halls. If photography restrictions are posted indoors, put your camera away in those areas.

rules.title: Recommended clothing for visiting the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear **clothing that covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a practical choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

faq: Is the White Temple an old Lanna temple?

It is a contemporary temple created by Chalermchai Kositpipat around Buddhist and mythological themes. Rather than a faithful restoration of an old building, it offers the artist’s expression in its white halls, sculptures and restroom building with a golden exterior.
What does the bridge to the main hall represent?

The bridge represents a journey from hell towards heaven. Crossing it in front of the white hall and seeing the sculptures along its sides are part of the artwork. Follow the route open to visitors across the bridge and around the hall.

wat-rong-suea-ten.name: Wat Rong Suea Ten
wat-rong-suea-ten.thai: วัดร่องเสือเต้น
wat-rong-suea-ten.type: Contemporary Buddhist temple with a blue hall
wat-rong-suea-ten.title: Wat Rong Suea Ten (Blue Temple): Chiang Rai Art and Visitor Guide | ThaiLiveNow
wat-rong-suea-ten.description: Wat Rong Suea Ten, the Blue Temple in Chiang Rai’s Rim Kok area, is known for its blue hall and naga guardians at the entrance. Its colour and sculpture offer a striking contrast with Wat Rong Khun, the White Temple.
intro: Wat Rong Suea Ten is Chiang Rai’s Blue Temple, with a large naga standing before its blue hall. The vivid building and curling sculptures at its entrance catch your eye together; look back and forth between the overall structure and its smaller decorations.

The hall in the Rim Kok area was created by a student of the artist behind the White Temple, while the naga design at the entrance was influenced by the craft of the artist behind the Black House. Look closely at the naga’s coiling body and head ornament in front of the blue building. If you are interested in contemporary art from Chiang Rai, the temple offers a chance to see distinct artistic approaches.

experiences.title: Follow the blue details around the hall
paragraphs: The nickname “Blue Temple” comes from the vivid blue exterior of the hall. First take in the building’s strong colour from a distance, then come closer to look at the details around the doors and eaves. Sculpted forms continue across the blue-painted surfaces.

Sculptures inspired by Buddhism and mythology appear throughout the building. Alongside the traditional temple roof form, you can see vivid colour and contemporary decorative expression. It also suits visitors who want to photograph striking architecture.

experiences.title: The naga and the influence of another Chiang Rai artist
paragraphs: The large naga in front of the main hall is more than entrance decoration. The Tourism Authority says its design was inspired by the craft of Thawan Duchanee, who created the Black House Museum. After seeing the blue hall and gold patterns, look at the naga’s long, curving body to see how the work of the architect and another artist meets in one place.

Suranok, the creator of the Blue Temple, was also a student of Chalermchai, who created the White Temple. If you plan to visit both, look beyond the colours: the naga here also references another local artist’s work.

experiences.title: Meaning in blue and gold
paragraphs: The Blue Temple’s colour makes a vivid photograph, but it also symbolises Buddhist teaching. The Tourism Authority connects its sky-like blue to the Dhamma, the Buddha’s true teaching. Gold details stand out against the blue and define the lines of the hall.

After looking at the blue and gold patterns in the main hall, look again at the naga at the entrance. You can consider the meaning of the colours separately from the local artist’s sculptural style. This is why the Blue and White Temples are more than two temples distinguished only by colour.

rules.title: Recommended clothing for visiting the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear **clothing that covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a practical choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

accessSections.title: Rim Kok area, north of Chiang Rai
paragraphs: The temple is listed about 4 km from the city in the direction of the airport. Search for **Wat Rong Suea Ten** as your destination.

faq: Are the Blue Temple and White Temple in the same place?

No. They are separate temples in Chiang Rai. Suranok, creator of the Blue Temple hall, was a student of Chalermchai, who created the White Temple. The Blue Temple has a blue hall and a large naga at the entrance; the White Temple has white halls and a symbolic bridge.
Whose work influenced the naga at the entrance?

The Tourism Authority says it was inspired by the craft of Thawan Duchanee, the artist behind the Black House. After seeing the blue and gold patterns on the hall, look at the curved body and head decoration of the naga at the entrance.

wat-chalong.name: Wat Chalong
wat-chalong.type: Phuket Buddhist temple honouring revered monks
wat-chalong.title: Wat Chalong: Phuket Temple and Local Worship | ThaiLiveNow
wat-chalong.description: Wat Chalong is a Buddhist temple southwest of Phuket Town. Its formal name is Wat Chaithararam. Visit the halls honouring highly respected local monks and see the temple’s Buddhist architecture.
intro: Wat Chalong’s formal name is Wat Chaithararam. At this temple southwest of Phuket Town, you can see richly decorated halls as well as revered monk statues covered in layers of gold leaf offered by local people.

Luang Pho Chaem is remembered for helping residents during the unrest around the tin mines in 1876. Look at the traces of devotional offerings inside the halls, then explore a temple connected with Phuket’s local history before the island became known as a beach destination.

experiences.title: Luang Pho Chaem, who helped residents during the mining unrest
paragraphs: Wat Chalong’s formal name is Wat Chaithararam. The temple honours monks who helped residents during the unrest among Phuket’s tin-mine workers in 1876. The revered monk statues in the halls are more than decoration: they commemorate figures whom local people relied on at the time.

Luang Pho Chaem was also known for meditation practice and traditional medicine. The Tourism Authority of Thailand notes that King Rama V conferred a monastic title on him. His story brings together the island’s mining history and local religious life from before Phuket became known as a beach destination.

experiences.title: Layers of gold leaf show how people pay their respects
paragraphs: Layers of gold leaf offered by worshippers cover the monk statues. The surface is densely coated with gold leaf as people express gratitude and respect to the revered monks. After looking around the ornate architecture, take a quiet moment inside the hall to observe the ongoing acts of worship.
Give worshippers room when they pray or make offerings. If you take photographs, be mindful that these halls are active places of worship, not just displays of statues.

experiences.title: Visit the temple between Phuket Town and the beaches
paragraphs: The temple is about 8 km southwest of Phuket Town. It is a separate trip from the Old Town streets or Patong Beach, so it is practical to plan the order of your visit around where you are staying.

If you want to visit after spending time at the beach, travel in time for the temple’s daytime visiting hours. You can explore the halls inside and out and quietly observe local people paying respects to the monk statues.

rules.title: Recommended clothing for visiting the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear **clothing that covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a practical choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

accessSections.title: Find Wat Chaithararam southwest of Phuket Town
paragraphs: The temple’s formal name is **Wat Chaithararam**. It is about 8 km southwest of Phuket Town. Search for **Wat Chalong / Wat Chaithararam, Phuket** on your map.

faq: Are Wat Chalong and Wat Chaithararam different temples?
They are the same temple. Wat Chaithararam is its formal name, and it is widely known as Wat Chalong. The temple is about 8 km southwest of Phuket Town.
Why are the monk statues in the halls covered with gold leaf?

Local people offered the gold leaf to express respect and gratitude to revered monks, including Luang Pho Chaem. He helped residents during the 1876 tin-mine unrest and was also known for meditation and traditional medicine.

safari-world.thai: ซาฟารีเวิลด์
safari-world.title: Safari World Bangkok: Safari Park, Marine Park and Visitor Guide | ThaiLiveNow
safari-world.description: In Safari Park, see giraffes, zebras and white rhinos from your vehicle; in Marine Park, walk among the Giraffe Terrace, animal exhibits and show venues. See opening hours and schedules for shows, safari coaches and feeding.
intro: Safari World, on the outskirts of Bangkok, combines a vehicle safari with a walk-through zoo. In Safari Park, drive your own car or ride the park’s coach past giraffes, zebras and white rhinos. In Marine Park, walk between show venues and exhibits featuring birds, land animals and aquatic life.

With children, watch giraffes and zebras from the vehicle, visit Giraffe Terrace and the bird exhibits, and choose a dolphin or stunt show. It suits families who want to combine a wildlife drive, a walk-through zoo and shows in one day.
facts: According to the official show schedule: Tuesday–Friday **09:00–16:30**; weekends and public holidays **09:00–17:00**
According to the official show schedule: Tuesday–Friday **09:00–17:00**; weekends and public holidays **09:00–17:30**
Weekday and weekend sessions differ. A revised schedule for the visit date is available at the ticket counter or information desk.

experiences.title: A safari through the window of your vehicle
paragraphs: Safari Park is a drive-through area designed to resemble the African savanna. Pass giraffes, zebras, deer, antelope and white rhinos, then continue to areas with lions, tigers and bears. Unlike standing in front of one enclosure, the animals and scenery change as your vehicle moves along, so look out for what appears beyond the window.

You can drive your **own car or take the park’s safari coach**. Coaches leave at scheduled times, so visitors without a car can also take the drive-through route. Check the coach departure times alongside the Marine Park show schedule when planning your day.

experiences.title: See giraffes close up at Giraffe Terrace
paragraphs: At **Giraffe Terrace** in Marine Park, stand on the terrace and see giraffes at close range. It offers a different distance and viewpoint from looking at them through the window of a safari vehicle.
There is also an activity where you can feed giraffes directly. If you take part, follow staff instructions on how to feed them.

experiences.title: Marine Park is more than an aquarium
paragraphs: Besides dolphin and sea lion show venues, Marine Park has Eggs World, a Madagascar lemur exhibit, a parrot walk and a seal area. Birds such as macaws, flamingos and scarlet ibises are among the attractions, as are tapirs, manatees and walruses. Walk between the exhibits and venues to see different kinds of animals.

Eggs World presents bird eggs and the hatching process. If your child enjoys birds and small animals, visit an exhibit between shows. There is also a large freshwater fish display, so you can see birds, land animals and aquatic life.

experiences.title: Choose sessions for animal and stunt shows
paragraphs: The operator’s schedule lists shows featuring orangutans, sea lions, elephants, dolphins and birds, alongside Cowboy Stunt and Spy War. You need to walk to the next venue after each show. Instead of rushing to see everything, choose the shows your group most wants to see so you have time for Marine Park’s exhibits too.

Seven kinds of show run at different times Tuesday to Friday, while some sessions increase on weekends and public holidays. For example, weekend dolphin shows are at 13:45 and 16:15. You can visit other animal exhibits in the morning and choose an afternoon show.

experiences.title: Animal feeding and the River Safari boat
paragraphs: Feeding activities are available for animals including giraffes, lorikeets, sun conures, pelicans, capybaras, elephants and camels. A River Safari boat route follows the waterway, giving you more activities to consider as you explore the animal exhibits.

Giraffe feeding is listed until 16:30 Tuesday to Friday and 17:00 on weekends and public holidays. The River Safari boat is a separate route operating from 10:30. Add these activities between exhibits and shows, checking what is included in your ticket product.

experiences.title: Places to eat between shows
paragraphs: Marine Park has restaurants such as Lion’s Den Restaurant, Waterside Food Court and Blossom Restaurant. Plan to eat after a bird or dolphin show before heading to another exhibit. The official map also marks snack and drink stalls and restrooms.

rules.title: Ticket products differ in which areas and activities they include
paragraphs: **To visit both Safari Park and Marine Park, you need a ticket that includes both areas.** If you do not have a car and want to take the safari route, also check whether a coach ride is included or needs to be arranged. Coach rides, feeding and boat trips depend on your booking’s inclusions.

faq: How are Safari Park and Marine Park different?

In Safari Park, drive your own car or take the coach through areas with giraffes, zebras, white rhinos and predators. Marine Park is a walk-through area with Giraffe Terrace, animal exhibits and show venues. Ticket products may include one or both areas.
Can I visit Safari Park without my own car?
Yes. You can take the park’s safari coach around the route. It leaves at scheduled times; see the coach departure schedule above.
Is Safari World open on Mondays?
The official operating information lists Tuesday to Sunday as open and Monday as closed.
What time can I feed the giraffes?
The operator lists giraffe feeding from 09:00–16:30 Tuesday to Friday and 09:00–17:00 on Saturday, Sunday and public holidays. Giraffe feeding is a separate activity from the show schedule.

intro: Khao Kheow Open Zoo is a large open-range zoo in Bang Phra, Si Racha, Chonburi. Its different areas feature animals ranging from giraffes and white rhinos to pygmy hippos and ring-tailed lemurs.

The zoo is also known for Moo Deng, a pygmy hippo born in 2024. Scheduled programmes between exhibits include elephant swimming and a penguin parade; transport inside the zoo is charged separately from admission. Its location and scale differ from Pattaya’s walkable central attractions.

experiences.title: From giraffes and white rhinos to sloths and lemurs
paragraphs: See giraffes, white rhinos, deer and a family of hippos, then visit areas with two-toed sloths and ring-tailed lemurs. The zoo’s featured animals also include giant anteaters, capybaras and wombats.

Ring-tailed lemurs live in an island-like enclosure surrounded by water. Viewing the regular exhibits is different from feeding animals or taking part in a closer-contact activity. Join feeding or contact experiences only in the areas allowed that day and as staff direct.

experiences.title: Moo Deng and her pygmy hippo family
paragraphs: Moo Deng, a pygmy hippo born here on 10 July 2024, became known for her energetic movements and daily antics. Her parents are Tony and Jona, and her sibling is Mu Tun. If you visit to see Moo Deng, it is also useful to know the names of her hippo family and that they are individual animals of the same species.

experiences.title: An elephant swimming and penguins coming out to walk
paragraphs: During the elephant swimming programme, watch elephants through the glass of a large tank. See how these big animals move and swim underwater. The penguin parade offers a different kind of viewing, as penguins walk out in a line.

Elephant swimming is viewed through the window of a large tank; the penguin parade is a scheduled walk by the penguins. The programmes take place in different areas, so consider their start times and the time needed to move between them.

experiences.title: Choose areas to explore instead of rushing around the entire zoo
paragraphs: Behind the visitor areas are spaces for wildlife conservation, education and research. Not all of the zoo is open to visitors; some areas are restricted to support research and conservation. If you are visiting with children, allow enough time to observe the animals that interest you and read the information.

The zoo lists golf carts, electric sightseeing trains, trams and EV three-wheelers for travelling between exhibits. Their charges differ, whether by ride or by two-hour rental, so choose how you want to get around the large grounds.

rules.title: Transport and animal experiences cost extra
paragraphs: Admission, transport such as carts, electric trains and trams, and separate feeding or contact experiences are different ticket items. You can use transport inside the zoo if it is difficult for anyone in your group to walk far.
Golf carts are listed at 500–700 baht per vehicle for two hours. Each cart has a passenger limit and return time; conditions may apply if you keep it beyond two hours.

faq: Is Khao Kheow Open Zoo in central Pattaya?
No. It is a large zoo in Bang Phra, Si Racha, Chonburi. Allow separate return travel from Pattaya; inside the zoo you can choose transport such as carts or trams.
What kind of animal is Moo Deng?

Moo Deng is a pygmy hippopotamus born at this zoo on 10 July 2024. Her parents are Tony and Jona, and her sibling is Mu Tun. Other zoo areas feature giraffes, white rhinos, sloths and ring-tailed lemurs.
When are elephant swimming and the penguin parade?

According to the official schedule for 19–25 October 2026, elephant swimming is at 11:00 and 14:30 on weekdays, and at 11:00, 12:30 and 14:30 on Saturday and Sunday. The penguin parade is at 10:00 and 14:00 on weekdays, with an additional 15:30 session on weekends. Public holidays and other weeks may have different times.
Is zoo cart hire included in admission?
No. Cart hire is separate from admission. The listed rate is 500–700 baht per vehicle for two hours; electric sightseeing trains, trams and EV three-wheelers have different rates.

chiang-mai-zoo.description: Chiang Mai Zoo is at the foot of Doi Suthep. It has expansive animal-viewing areas and a separate aquarium, so check which facilities are covered by basic admission and which need an additional ticket.
intro: Chiang Mai Zoo is an outdoor zoo at the foot of Doi Suthep, with exhibits including capybaras, kangaroos and penguins. An aquarium in the grounds has freshwater and marine displays linked by underwater tunnels.

The standard zoo visit, aquarium and transport around the grounds are separate items on the price list. You need a separate aquarium ticket to see the tanks. Chiang Mai Zoo is also a different place from Chiang Mai Night Safari, which offers evening vehicle tours.

experiences.title: A new capybara exhibit and animals at the foot of the mountain
paragraphs: Chiang Mai Zoo began as Harold Mason Young’s private zoo and is now run by the Zoological Park Organization of Thailand. It covers a large area at the foot of Doi Suthep, with animal exhibits spread across the grounds.

In 2025, the zoo introduced a new capybara exhibit with more shade and living space. The same year, its information also featured areas for red kangaroos, penguins, red-shanked doucs and pygmy goats. Families who want to spend time observing animals can plan around the areas that interest them.

experiences.title: Feeding activities and behind-the-scenes experiences
paragraphs: The zoo’s 2025 information listed feeding activities with hippopotamuses, deer and Asian elephants, as well as behind-the-scenes programmes with penguins, ring-tailed lemurs and capybaras. You can choose between viewing animals in their exhibits and taking part in a closer activity with staff guidance.

These feeding and behind-the-scenes programmes are separate from the general exhibits. Some require advance booking, so distinguish programme participation from viewing animals at the tanks or enclosures.

experiences.title: A separate aquarium known as the sea on the mountain
paragraphs: The Chiang Mai Zoo Aquarium in the grounds has freshwater and marine exhibits connected by an underwater tunnel. After seeing land animals outdoors, you can go inside to explore creatures from rivers and the sea.

Walk through the tunnel between freshwater and marine exhibits after visiting the outdoor animal areas. Standard zoo admission, aquarium admission and transport within the grounds are separate charges. The aquarium is also separate from Chiang Mai Night Safari, so plan the route independently if visiting both in one day.

rules.title: Golf carts are rented by the hour
paragraphs: Zoo admission, transport vehicles inside the grounds and the separate aquarium are different fare items. A golf cart is listed at **350 baht per vehicle per hour**.

The official fare list in English and Thai shows different tram prices, so a single fare cannot be stated with confidence. If you are travelling with someone who finds it difficult to get around, decide whether to use a cart or tram, and ask the ticket office which fare applies to international visitors before boarding the tram.

faq: Are Chiang Mai Zoo and Night Safari the same place?
No. Chiang Mai Zoo is an outdoor zoo on Huay Kaew Road at the foot of Doi Suthep. Night Safari is a separate attraction with vehicle routes through savanna and predator areas.
Does a zoo ticket include the aquarium?
Standard zoo admission and the aquarium ticket are separate items. The aquarium in the zoo grounds has a tunnel connecting freshwater and marine exhibits.
How are children’s tickets priced?
The zoo price list gives a 120-baht child ticket for visitors under 135 cm and a 350-baht standard adult ticket.
How much does a golf cart cost?
The zoo’s official services information lists golf carts at 350 baht per vehicle per hour. This is separate from zoo admission.

chiang-mai-night-safari.description: Chiang Mai Night Safari has vehicle-based animal viewing and walk-through areas. Its vehicle routes are divided into the herbivore-focused Savanna Safari and Predator Prowl, which features predator habitats.
intro: At Chiang Mai Night Safari, vehicle routes pass through Savanna Safari, an herbivore zone, and Predator Prowl, a predator zone. One route features animals such as giraffes and zebras; the other focuses on tigers and lions.

Outside the vehicle routes, there are walking exhibits and shows. Chiang Mai Night Safari is a different venue from Chiang Mai Zoo near Doi Suthep and has separate tickets. Choose among the vehicle routes, walking exhibits and shows included in your booking.

experiences.title: Look for giraffes and zebras on Savanna Safari
paragraphs: On Savanna Safari, stay in the vehicle as you travel through the herbivore zone. Giraffes, zebras and red kangaroos are among the featured animals. Instead of walking up to the animals, you look out of the vehicle as it passes through their habitat.

experiences.title: Predator Prowl, featuring tigers and lions
paragraphs: Predator Prowl is a predator-viewing route separate from the savanna route. It features animals such as tigers and lions, so even though both trips are by vehicle, they cover different zones and themes.
The two vehicle routes offer different kinds of viewing. Animals are not always active at night, so follow staff guidance and observe what is visible on the day from inside the vehicle.

experiences.title: Add walking exhibits and shows between vehicle routes
paragraphs: In addition to the Savanna Safari and Predator Prowl vehicle routes, there are walking exhibits and shows. The vehicle routes take you through animal zones, while in the walking areas you can stop in front of an exhibit. The routes and shows may be included in different booking packages.

Vehicle departures and shows each run at set times. Arrive in line with your booked date and start time, and allow a little time between waiting for a vehicle and getting to the show venue. Chiang Mai Night Safari is a different facility from Chiang Mai Zoo near Doi Suthep, with separate tickets.

rules.title: Check your booked time and programme names
paragraphs: Review the **visit date, start time, vehicle tour and included shows** on your booking confirmation. This is a different product from a Chiang Mai Zoo ticket.

faq: Is Night Safari a zoo where you walk around the whole time?
No. Savanna Safari and Predator Prowl are vehicle routes, and there are separate walking exhibits and show areas.
What animals can I see on the two vehicle routes?
Savanna Safari focuses on herbivores such as giraffes, zebras and red kangaroos. Predator Prowl features predators such as tigers and lions. The routes cover different zones and themes.
Can I use a Chiang Mai Zoo ticket to enter Night Safari?
No. They are separate facilities. Chiang Mai Zoo is an open-air zoo at the foot of Doi Suthep, while Night Safari has its own vehicle routes and walking exhibits.

sea-life-bangkok.title: SEA LIFE Bangkok Ocean World: Exhibits, Feeding Times and Tickets | ThaiLiveNow
sea-life-bangkok.description: SEA LIFE Bangkok Ocean World is an indoor aquarium inside Siam Paragon in Bangkok. It suits visitors who want to pair marine-life exhibits with city shopping or families looking for an indoor activity with children.
intro: SEA LIFE Bangkok Ocean World is an indoor aquarium inside Siam Paragon. Explore different underwater environments from the coral reef, seahorse and jellyfish exhibits on B1 to the Ocean Tunnel and penguin area on B2.

Shark Walk, where you look down at sharks through a transparent floor, and the tunnel, where tanks extend overhead, offer different views. The Department of Fisheries’ Bangkok Aquarium is a separate facility in Bang Khen; set your destination to Siam Paragon for this aquarium.

experiences.title: Coral reef fish, seahorses and jellyfish on B1
paragraphs: On B1, exhibits explore different environments, including coral reefs, rainforest and jellyfish. The reef area features brightly coloured fish such as clownfish, while the seahorse area shows how seahorses use their tails to hold onto seaweed as they feed.

The seahorse exhibit explains how they grip seaweed with their tails, while the jellyfish area lets you watch their transparent bodies move through the water. From clownfish on the reef to aquatic plants in the rainforest display, the exhibits change from one environment to another even on B1.

experiences.title: Look down at sharks, then look up in the tunnel
paragraphs: At Shark Walk, look down through a transparent acrylic floor at the shark tank below. Find sharks swimming beneath your feet: this display lets you see them from above, unlike viewing them from beside the tank.

In the Ocean Tunnel on B2, tanks extend above and beside the walkway. Compared with Shark Walk, where you look through the floor, the tunnel gives you a completely different view of the same large fish.

experiences.title: Gentoo penguins, a rocky shore and starfish
paragraphs: The Penguin Ice Playground on B2 features gentoo penguins. The Rocky Shore area separately presents turtles and African penguins. Although both displays include penguins, they feature different species in separate environments.
At Rockpool, you can take a close look at starfish in several types of tank. A close-up display does not automatically mean you may touch the animals; follow the contact instructions for each tank.

experiences.title: Choose between the aquarium and additional experiences
paragraphs: The operator recommends allowing at least 90 minutes to visit the aquarium. Set aside time for the exhibits on each floor rather than treating it as a quick stop between shopping at Siam Paragon, so you can explore from the seahorses to the tunnel and penguins without rushing.

Alongside standard aquarium admission, combined products such as a boat ride or 4D experience are sold. What is included varies by ticket. Viewing the feeding sessions included with admission is also different from a paid behind-the-scenes tour. An advertised starting price does not necessarily apply to every adult or experience.

rules.title: Last admission is one hour before closing
paragraphs: The dedicated opening-hours information lists **last admission at 19:00 and closing at 20:00**. If visiting in the evening, arrive before the last admission time.

rules.title: Check the ticket type for adults and children
paragraphs: Do not treat the lowest online price as the adult admission price. Select your visit date and the number of adults and children, then confirm whether the ticket covers standard admission or a package with additional activities before paying.

faq: What exhibits can I see at SEA LIFE Bangkok?

B1 has coral reef, seahorse, jellyfish and rainforest exhibits, as well as Shark Walk with its transparent floor. On B2, you can see the Ocean Tunnel and exhibits featuring gentoo and African penguins.
What time is last admission?
The official visiting hours are 10:00–20:00, with last admission at 19:00. The aquarium recommends allowing at least 90 minutes for your visit.
Are the feeding sessions included with admission?
The official programme schedule marks shark, gentoo penguin, otter, ray and African penguin feeding sessions as included with admission. Days and times vary by animal.
Is the behind-the-scenes tour included with a standard ticket?

The Beyond the Surface tour is a separate experience costing 390 baht per person in addition to admission. It is available to visitors aged 3 and over; children aged 3–11 must be accompanied by an adult. Reserve a timed slot with available capacity at the activity counter.

underwater-world-pattaya.description: Underwater World Pattaya is an aquarium on Sukhumvit Road. Walk through its 105-metre transparent tunnel, with separate coral reef, shark and ray, and giant freshwater fish sections.
intro: Underwater World Pattaya’s approximately 105-metre transparent tunnel passes from the coral reef through the shark-and-ray Open Ocean to a zone for large Thai freshwater fish. It is an indoor visit on Sukhumvit Road, separate from sightseeing on Pattaya Beach.
Outside the tunnel, there are a touch pool, Magic Tank, reptile and otter exhibits. Diver feeding sessions are viewing programmes; activities where visitors feed animals themselves are separate.
facts: 320 baht · Check the height cutoff at the ticket office

experiences.title: A tunnel from coral reef to sharks and giant freshwater fish
paragraphs: The approximately 105-metre transparent tunnel is divided into different themed zones: Coral Reef, Open Ocean and Giant of Siam. The reef area features colourful tropical fish, while Open Ocean highlights blacktip reef sharks, jacks and large groupers.

After the marine exhibits, Giant of Siam presents large freshwater fish in a shipwreck-themed setting. With children, compare the sharks you saw earlier with the big freshwater fish here. The tunnel takes you through displays of both sea and river life.

experiences.title: The touch pool and Magic Tank offer different experiences
paragraphs: The touch pool recreates rocky pools on the Thai coast, where visitors can encounter marine life. Magic Tank is presented as a separate interactive tank. Beyond the tunnel, there are also reptile and otter exhibits, so the aquarium is more than one long passage.

Take part in hands-on contact only in the designated pool and follow staff instructions. General display tanks are not for touching or adding food. If visiting with young children, read the signs at each tank first and choose an activity that is allowed there.

experiences.title: Diver feeding sessions and visitor feeding are different activities
paragraphs: You can watch feeding sessions in the Coral Reef, Open Ocean and Giant of Siam tanks. Divers feed animals in each of these separate tanks, so choose the session for the exhibit you want to see. Explore the aquarium freely and go to the relevant tank for its start time.

Visitors can also feed fish and turtles themselves as a separate activity. This differs from watching divers feed animals inside the tanks. Touch-pool and feeding experiences are available only in designated areas with staff guidance; check whether the activity and its fee are included in your ticket, separately from general admission.

rules.title: Take part in activities only in designated areas
paragraphs: For animal contact or feeding, follow **staff guidance in areas where the activity is permitted**. Do not treat regular exhibit tanks as activity areas.

faq: What zones are connected by the 105-metre tunnel?
The tunnel passes through the Coral Reef, Open Ocean with sharks and rays, and Giant of Siam, where you can see large freshwater fish. It lets you view marine and river fish in sequence.
When can I watch the diver feeding sessions?

The published sessions are 10:30 and 15:00 at the Coral Reef tank, 11:00 and 16:00 at Open Ocean, and 11:30 and 15:30 at Giant of Siam. Each tank has different times, so plan around the exhibit you want to see.
What time is last admission?
The listed visiting hours are 09:00–18:00, with last admission at 17:30.
Can I touch or feed animals at any tank?
No. The touch pool is a designated activity area, and visitor feeding is also limited to specific locations. General display tanks are not for putting your hands or food into.
