aquaria-phuket.description: Aquaria Phuket is on Level B1 of Central Phuket Floresta. Explore freshwater habitats themed around forests and rivers, followed by coastal and ray exhibits and a large marine tank, each presenting a different underwater environment.
intro: Aquaria Phuket is on B1 of Central Phuket Floresta. Its exhibits move from freshwater fish in the Himmapan Forest to reptiles and otters, coastal penguins and rays, and a large marine tank.

This indoor aquarium inside the shopping centre is separate from Phuket Aquarium at Cape Panwa. Aquarium-only admission and the combined MAYA ticket are different products, and online tickets are listed for purchase at least three hours before your visit.
facts: At least **3 hours before your visit**

experiences.title: From the Himmapan Forest to river fish
paragraphs: Mystic Forest explores the Himmapan Forest of Thai mythology, with small and large freshwater fish and an underwater landscape with aquatic plants. The connected Canopy Walk offers views of freshwater fish in a space inspired by the tree canopy.

At Jewels of the Jungle, look at reptiles; River Cave recreates a flowing-water cave and features Asian small-clawed otters. After seeing freshwater fish in the Himmapan Forest, continue to the reptiles and otters.

experiences.title: Penguins and rays before the large marine exhibit
paragraphs: Coastal Haven presents penguins and sharks in a rocky coastal setting. Stingray Bay has exhibits devoted to coral and different rays, bringing together coastal environments and the movement of animals in the tanks.

South China Sea is the aquarium’s largest marine exhibit. After the freshwater fish and otters, walk to the large ocean tank. With children, look at each tank while recalling the animals you saw in rivers and at sea.

experiences.title: A shipwreck story, jellyfish and the touch pool
paragraphs: The Largato area also tells the story of the U.S.S. Largato, a vessel sunk in the Gulf of Thailand. Alongside the tank exhibits, you can learn about the shipwreck behind the display.

Station Aquarius has jellyfish exhibits and a touch pool. After looking at the jellyfish, you can join the activity permitted at the touch pool. Follow staff instructions in the designated area when handling marine life. Families interested in otters, reptiles and sea animals can set aside time to explore between shopping stops.

experiences.title: Choose an aquarium-only ticket or a ticket including MAYA
paragraphs: The aquarium is on B1 of Central Phuket Floresta. The official sales page lists Aquarium Only and a combined ticket that includes the MAYA Museum, so choose according to whether you want only the aquarium or another exhibit as well.

Online tickets are listed for purchase at least three hours before your visit. Aquarium Only and the MAYA combination cover different attractions, and online bookings cannot be cancelled, refunded or changed. Decide on your date, group size and the applicable height category for children before choosing a ticket.

rules.title: Do not leave an online ticket purchase until arrival
paragraphs: Official online tickets are listed for purchase at least three hours before your visit. A ticket ordered just before arrival is not guaranteed to be ready for immediate use.

rules.title: Choose a ticket using the child’s height
paragraphs: Children’s tickets are sold by height category. Aquarium-only and MAYA combination tickets are also different products, so select the option that matches the child’s height and the attractions you plan to visit on the checkout screen.

rules.title: Online tickets cannot be cancelled, refunded or changed
paragraphs: Official online bookings cannot be cancelled, refunded or changed. Confirm your date and party size before purchasing, at least three hours before your visit.

faq: Are Aquaria Phuket and Phuket Aquarium the same place?
No. Aquaria Phuket is on B1 of Central Phuket Floresta. Phuket Aquarium is a separate marine research facility at Cape Panwa.
What comes after the Himmapan Forest exhibit?

The route continues from freshwater fish to reptiles and otters, then coastal exhibits with penguins and rays, South China Sea’s large marine tank, and Station Aquarius with jellyfish and a touch pool.
Can I buy an online ticket just before my visit?
Official guidance says to purchase at least three hours before visiting. Online bookings cannot be cancelled, refunded or changed, and Aquarium Only and the MAYA combination are different products.
How much is an official aquarium-only ticket?

The official listing shows standard foreign-visitor Aquarium Only prices of 1,390 baht for adults and 750 baht for children. At the time shown, a discount was displayed at 1,251 baht and 675 baht; the amount payable is the one shown at checkout. The MAYA combination is a different product.

phuket-aquarium.description: Phuket Aquarium is operated by a marine-resource research institute at Cape Panwa. See marine life in its underwater tunnel and display tanks, and learn about marine resources and environmental conservation.
intro: Phuket Aquarium is an educational aquarium run by a marine research institute at Cape Panwa. Its underwater tunnel and display tanks introduce marine life alongside information about marine resources and conservation.

The exhibits include a touch pool, diver feeding sessions, animation and a robotic mermaid. This is a different facility, operator and location from Aquaria Phuket inside Central Phuket shopping centre.

experiences.title: A Cape Panwa aquarium with a research history
paragraphs: Phuket Aquarium has displayed marine life since 1983. Run by a marine research institute, it combines tanks for observing living animals with information about marine resources and conservation.
At the Cape Panwa exhibits, read about the animals’ names and habitats as well as marine conservation. The underwater tunnel and a 12-sided display tank make this more than a single-tank visit.

experiences.title: Watch the animals and divers in the tunnel tank
paragraphs: The tunnel tank gives you a close view of underwater life. If you arrive during a diver feeding session, you can watch divers feed the animals. Notice how the animals move when divers enter a tank you were viewing moments earlier.

The aquarium also features a 12-sided display tank. Take time to observe how the underwater scene differs from tank to tank rather than passing through quickly. Unlike viewing the exhibits at your own pace, feeding sessions take place at set times.

experiences.title: A touch pool, animation and a robotic mermaid
paragraphs: At the touch pool, you can observe seafloor animals at close range and learn about their behaviour. Not every animal is available to touch, so take part only in the way allowed in that area.

After viewing the tanks, look for the underwater-world exhibit with animation and a robotic mermaid from the Yeosu Expo in Korea. Alongside living animals, children can see educational displays using video and robotics.

rules.title: Check the difference between holiday promotions and general admission
paragraphs: The government’s year-end **free admission promotion for Thai visitors** applies only to specified visitors and dates. Do not treat it as the regular admission price for travellers from other countries.

faq: Is Phuket Aquarium the same as Aquaria Phuket in the mall?
No. Phuket Aquarium is the research-institute aquarium at Cape Panwa. Aquaria Phuket is a separate aquarium on B1 of Central Phuket Floresta.
When can I watch diver feeding?
The published schedule lists tunnel-tank diver feeding daily from 11:00 to 11:30. It is a viewing programme where divers feed aquatic animals inside the tank.
What else is there besides the tunnel?
The exhibits include a 12-sided display tank, touch pool, underwater-world animation and a robotic mermaid from the Yeosu Expo in Korea. Follow the rules posted for the touch pool.

chatuchak-market.name: Chatuchak Market
chatuchak-market.thai: ตลาดนัดจตุจักร
chatuchak-market.type: Weekend market for clothing, accessories and crafts
chatuchak-market.title: Chatuchak Weekend Market: Shopping Areas and Visitor Guide | ThaiLiveNow
chatuchak-market.description: At Bangkok’s Chatuchak Market, walk from clothing and bag stalls to vintage goods, art and furniture. Weekend shopping, the Thursday–Friday plant market and Friday night retail hours run on different schedules.
intro: Chatuchak is a large Bangkok weekend market where different sections feature clothing, vintage items, art, furniture and plants. The market moved here from a square in front of the Grand Palace in 1982. Today, there are also many places to eat alongside the stalls.

Browse clothes and bags in Sections 2–4 and vintage items in Sections 5–6. If you are looking for art or furnishings, continue to Sections 7 and 25–26. The clock tower is a useful landmark for finding your way between sections.

experiences.title: Sections for clothing and vintage finds
paragraphs: The market guide identifies Sections 2–4 for fashion and Sections 5–6 for vintage goods. A few sections away from streets full of clothing, bags and accessories, you will find stalls selling second-hand and older items.
Make a note of the section number for a shop you like so you can find it again after browsing elsewhere. The market is large, and it is easy to lose track of where you saw a particular kind of stall.

experiences.title: Art, ceramics and furniture sections
paragraphs: Section 7 features art such as paintings; Sections 25–26 have ceramics, furniture and other home décor. Leave the clothing stalls behind to browse art and household goods.
The clock tower in the centre of the market is a useful landmark as you move between sections. It is also an easy place to meet up after exploring different stalls with your group.

experiences.title: Weekend shopping and plant-market days
paragraphs: Alongside the weekend market for clothing and crafts, a plant market is listed for Thursday and Friday, with Friday evening retail hours focused on shops. The stalls and goods available vary by day, even at the same location.

On Thursdays and Fridays, shoppers looking for potted plants and gardening items gather in the plant section. Unlike the weekend route for clothing, vintage goods, art and furniture, the focus on those days is choosing plants.

rules.title: Check the schedule for each section and shop
paragraphs: The weekend market on Saturday and Sunday, the plant market on Thursday and Friday, and Friday night retail hours each have different listed schedules. Individual shops in a section may not all open and close at the same time.

accessSections.title: Travel to the market by train
paragraphs: You can reach the market from Kamphaeng Phet or Chatuchak Park stations on the MRT, and Mo Chit station on the BTS. The market is extensive and goods vary by section, so check the map for the locations you want to see, such as clothing in Section 2–4 or art in Section 7.

faq: Can I visit Chatuchak only at weekends?

The weekend market for clothing and crafts is listed as open Saturday and Sunday, 09:00–18:00. The plant market is listed Thursday and Friday, 07:00–18:00; Friday night retail hours are 18:00–24:00. Individual shops may keep different hours.
Where can I find clothing and vintage items?

The market guide lists fashion goods such as clothing and bags in Sections 2–4 and vintage items in Sections 5–6. For art, visit Section 7; for ceramics, furniture and home décor, look in Sections 25–26.
Which train station should I use?
You can use Kamphaeng Phet or Chatuchak Park on the MRT, or Mo Chit on the BTS. The market is large, so choose your approach based on the section you plan to visit.

or-tor-kor-market.name: Or Tor Kor Market
or-tor-kor-market.type: Market for fruit, ingredients and prepared food
or-tor-kor-market.title: Or Tor Kor Market Bangkok: Fruit, Food and Visitor Guide | ThaiLiveNow
or-tor-kor-market.description: Or Tor Kor is a Bangkok food market operated by the Marketing Organization for Farmers. Under one roof, find fruit, vegetables, seafood and dried goods, along with prepared food and a dining area.
intro: Or Tor Kor is a Bangkok food market operated by the Marketing Organization for Farmers. Under its roof are stalls selling fruit and vegetables, meat and seafood, dried goods and rice, as well as prepared side dishes and places to eat.

Browse the fruit and vegetables at the stalls, choose rice snacks or prepared dishes, then have a meal in the dining area. Across the road, Chatuchak is known for clothing and crafts; at Or Tor Kor, you will find ingredients and foods served at Thai tables.
facts: Marketing Organization for Farmers of Thailand (Or Tor Kor)

experiences.title: Produce and ingredients under one roof
paragraphs: Under the broad roof are stalls selling fruit and vegetables, and shops handling meat, seafood, dried goods and rice. You can see the fish and produce used in Thai dishes that you may have eaten at restaurants.

The market sells produce selected by the Marketing Organization for Farmers, making the fruit and vegetable stalls interesting to browse. Fruit varieties and stock differ by shop and day, so you may notice seasonal changes in what is on display.

experiences.title: Buy prepared dishes or eat at the market
paragraphs: Past the ingredient shops, you will also find prepared side dishes, rice snacks and sweets. You can take the side dishes away, or have breakfast or lunch in the dining area.

Under the same roof, you can browse fresh fruit and vegetables, shops selling meat, seafood, dried goods and rice, and stalls serving cooked food. Shopping for ingredients and eating a prepared meal are both possible in the market.

experiences.title: Visit alongside Chatuchak
paragraphs: After browsing clothing and crafts at Chatuchak, cross the road to Or Tor Kor for fruit, dried-goods stalls and places to eat. The two markets offer different goods, so it is easy to combine shopping and a meal.

accessSections.title: Market on Kamphaeng Phet Road
paragraphs: The address is **101 Kamphaeng Phet Road**. Access via Kamphaeng Phet MRT Station is listed.

faq: Is Or Tor Kor part of Chatuchak Market?

No. Or Tor Kor is a food market operated by the Marketing Organization for Farmers, while Chatuchak is known as a weekend market for clothing, crafts and other goods. The two markets are close across the road, so you can visit both.
Can I eat at the market?
Yes. In addition to stalls selling fruit and vegetables, meat, seafood and dried goods, there are prepared dishes and a dining area. You can take side dishes away or eat breakfast or lunch there.
What time can I visit?
The market’s listed hours are approximately 06:00–20:00. Individual shops and restaurants may keep different hours.

khlong-lat-mayom-floating-market.title: Khlong Lat Mayom Floating Market: Food and Canal Visit Guide | ThaiLiveNow
khlong-lat-mayom-floating-market.description: Khlong Lat Mayom is a weekend market beside a canal in Bang Ramat, western Bangkok, with land-based food stalls and shops selling everyday goods. Eat grilled fish or noodles, then walk through the waterside market without taking a boat.
intro: Khlong Lat Mayom is a weekend community market along a canal in Bang Ramat, western Bangkok, with food stalls and shops selling everyday goods. The land-based market and places to eat run alongside the waterway, so you can enjoy a visit without taking a boat.

Choose a meal such as grilled fish, boat noodles or khanom chin, then try a sweet like khanom ko or some fruit. You can also browse shops selling straw hats, woven bags and herbal products to see the market’s mix of food and everyday goods.

experiences.title: Grilled food and noodles by the canal
paragraphs: Land-based stalls and waterside dining areas offer grilled fish and seafood, som tam, grilled chicken and several kinds of noodles. You can choose a bowl of boat noodles or khanom chin for a meal.
Even when you see boats on the water, you do not need to board one to eat or shop at the market. You can walk and enjoy the scene of the canal beside the stalls.

experiences.title: Sweets and handmade goods
paragraphs: After your meal, look for khanom ko, a sweet made with coconut and sesame. The market information also lists pomelo, bananas and coconuts among the fruit.

There are shops selling straw hats, woven bags and herbal products too. Rather than eating and leaving straight away, browse the land-based stalls for clothing, pottery and household goods to see another side of this community market.

experiences.title: Canal boat tours are a separate option
paragraphs: A sightseeing trip along the canal is separate from walking around the market. If you want to see more of the area from the water, check the route and return point at the pier. You do not need to board a boat if you are visiting for the market food and land-based shops.
Boat trips may use different routes and fare units. Before boarding, check whether the quoted price is per person or per boat, as well as passenger limits, duration, stops and extra costs.

rules.title: Boat trips are separate from walking around the market
paragraphs: You can walk to the land-based shops and waterside dining areas. If you take a boat, check whether the quoted fare is per person or per boat, along with the passenger limit, operating time, stops and additional costs.

faq: Do I have to take a boat to visit the market?
No. You can walk through the land-based market, with stalls selling food, fruit and everyday goods, and eat beside the canal. A canal boat tour is a separate activity you can choose.
What food can I try?

The market features grilled fish and seafood, som tam and grilled chicken, as well as noodles such as boat noodles and khanom chin. After eating, look around the khanom ko sweets and fruit stalls too.
When is it open?
The market is listed as open on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays from 08:00 to 17:00. Individual stalls may start and close at different times.

amphawa-floating-market.name: Amphawa Floating Market

amphawa-floating-market.type: Weekend floating market with shops along both sides of a canal
amphawa-floating-market.title: Amphawa Floating Market: Canal Walk, Food and Firefly Boats | ThaiLiveNow
amphawa-floating-market.description: Amphawa Floating Market is a weekend market in Samut Songkhram, with wooden houses, food boats and shops along both sides of a canal. Cross the arched bridge to enjoy grilled seafood and snacks.
intro: Amphawa is a weekend market in Samut Songkhram, with wooden houses and shops along both sides of a canal. From the arched bridge, look down at food boats moored by the water and the two market streets, then cross to continue to shops on the other side.

Have grilled seafood, then try oliang iced coffee or coconut ice cream for an evening by the canal. Firefly boat trips after sunset are a separate activity from walking around the market. Whether wild fireflies are visible depends on the natural conditions that day.
facts: Friday, Saturday, Sunday and public holidays

experiences.title: A market between wooden houses and an arched bridge
paragraphs: Wooden houses and shops line both sides of the canal, connected by an arched bridge. From the bridge, you can see the moored food boats and steps down to the water.

On one waterside lane, browse shop displays up close; cross the bridge to continue to restaurants and stalls on the opposite side. Unlike an indoor market with all its aisles inside a building, this market spreads out along the canal and lanes.

experiences.title: Seafood grilled on boats and market snacks
paragraphs: Choose grilled seafood from a boat moored by the water, then eat near the steps along the canal. Thai coffee, seasonal fruit and coconut ice cream are also among the market treats.
After a meal, browse shops selling textiles, wooden toys and jewellery. Food boats moored in front of the old wooden shophouses are part of Amphawa’s waterside market scene.

experiences.title: The weekend market and firefly boat trips
paragraphs: The market is open on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays. You can still see the canal and wooden houses on weekdays, but the weekend’s food boats and street stalls are not set up in the same way.

If you want to take a firefly boat trip after sunset, check the **departure point, route, fare and return time** separately. Fireflies are wild animals, so seeing them is not guaranteed just because you take a boat.

faq: Can I visit Amphawa outside the weekend?
The canal and village of wooden houses are still there on weekdays. However, the market with food boats and street stalls is listed as open on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays.
What food can I find at the market?
You can choose grilled seafood from boats moored by the water. Oliang iced coffee, coconut ice cream and seasonal fruit are also listed among the market’s treats.
Are firefly boat trips included in a market visit?
No. They are a separate boat activity after sunset. Check the departure point, route, fare and return time before deciding; wild fireflies may not be visible even if you take the trip.

mae-klong-railway-market.name: Mae Klong Railway Market
mae-klong-railway-market.thai: ตลาดร่มหุบ
mae-klong-railway-market.type: Market along an active railway line
mae-klong-railway-market.title: Mae Klong Railway Market: Train Times, Market and Safety | ThaiLiveNow
mae-klong-railway-market.description: Mae Klong Railway Market is a working market beside the active railway near Mae Klong Station in Samut Songkhram. Watch vendors fold back awnings as trains pass between stalls selling fish, vegetables and fruit.
intro: Mae Klong Railway Market is a working market beside the tracks used by trains to and from Mae Klong Station. At stalls selling pla tu fish, vegetables, fruit and curry paste, vendors respond to the train warning by folding back their awnings and moving goods away from the tracks. After the train passes, they put the awnings back and continue trading.

Walk along the railway-side fish and fruit stalls and watch the scene change as a train approaches. This visit suits people who want to see not only the train passing but also the market returning to its usual rhythm afterward.

experiences.title: A working market selling pla tu and daily ingredients
paragraphs: Stalls on either side of the tracks sell pla tu and other seafood, vegetables, fruit, curry paste and household goods. When there is no train, vendors continue selling their goods beneath the awnings. With family, walk past the fish and fruit stalls and see what Mae Klong residents come to buy.

The market’s Thai name, Talat Rom Hup, means ‘umbrella-closing market’. Its shopping lane follows the railway, with display stands close to the tracks, creating a scene unlike an ordinary market even when no train is passing.

experiences.title: Awnings folded back for the train, then set out again
paragraphs: When the train warning sounds, vendors move goods away from the tracks and fold back awnings and parasols. Once the last carriage has passed, they put the awnings back and bring out their displays again. You can watch the stalls return to business and welcome customers after the train has gone.

The practice of clearing the stalls for passing trains is said to date from around 1984. When there is no train, residents shop for ingredients and vendors continue trading under their awnings. The market alternates between a brief train passage and the everyday rhythm of shopping.

rules.title: Clear the track when a train approaches
paragraphs: This is an active railway. Follow **instructions from vendors and railway staff to clear the area**, and do not stay on the track to take photographs.

accessSections.title: Take a ferry at Mahachai when travelling by train from Bangkok
paragraphs: If travelling from Bangkok by train, go from **Wongwian Yai Station to Mahachai Station**, then cross the river by ferry towards Tha Chalom. From **Ban Laem Station, take the train to Mae Klong**. A river separates the two railway sections, so there is no single train directly from Bangkok to Mae Klong.

The journey involves travelling by train, then ferry and train again. If you also want to visit Amphawa Floating Market, you need separate transport from Mae Klong. The two markets open on different days, so coordinate your dates when planning both visits.

faq: What time do trains arrive at Mae Klong Market?

Under the State Railway of Thailand’s planned schedule, trains arrive at Mae Klong Station at 08:30, 11:10, 14:30 and 17:40 and depart at 06:20, 09:00, 11:30 and 15:30. These are station arrival and departure times, so the train passes individual stalls at different times. Delays and service changes are possible.
Can I take one train from Bangkok to Mae Klong?

No. Travel from Wongwian Yai Station to Mahachai Station, cross the river by ferry towards Tha Chalom, then take a train to Mae Klong from Ban Laem Station. The route combines two railway sections with a ferry crossing.
Can I visit the market when no train is passing?

Yes. It is a working market selling fish, seafood, fruit, vegetables, curry paste and other goods, not a facility built solely for train viewing. The market is listed as open 06:00–18:00, though individual stalls keep their own hours. When a train approaches, leave the tracks and stand in a safe place as vendors and staff direct.

chiang-mai-sunday-market.description: Chiang Mai Sunday Walking Street opens on Sunday evenings from Tha Phae Gate along Ratchadamnoen Road. Browse northern Thai crafts and incense, and try snacks such as khai pam or mango salad.
intro: Chiang Mai Sunday Walking Street stretches along Ratchadamnoen Road from Tha Phae Gate on Sunday evenings. Walk the Old City streets to browse northern Thai crafts, household goods and incense, then choose street food or fruit drinks.

Browse handmade soap, textiles and paintings, then try khai pam, an egg dish cooked in a banana-leaf cup, or mango salad. Saturday’s Wua Lai Market and the daily Chang Khlan Night Bazaar are in different locations, leaving Ratchadamnoen with its own Sunday market scene.

experiences.title: Northern Thai crafts along Ratchadamnoen Road
paragraphs: On Sunday evenings, stalls line Ratchadamnoen Road from Tha Phae Gate towards Wat Phra Singh. Walk along a street inside the Old City and take in northern crafts alongside the historic cityscape.
Stalls sell different goods, from handmade soap, dolls, pillowcases and paintings to clothing and shoes. If you enjoy incense or textiles, take a look at the materials and patterns as you walk.

experiences.title: Khai pam and market snacks
paragraphs: Choose something filling for dinner or a small snack to try as you walk. Khai pam is an egg dish cooked in a banana-leaf cup. You may also find mango salad with crispy fish, peanuts and herbs.
There are also fried wontons with filling, fruit and herbal drinks. Pick a snack you can eat as you walk, such as khai pam, and spend the evening browsing the craft stalls.

experiences.title: A Sunday evening on the street
paragraphs: The market section described by the Tourism Authority runs about 1 kilometre along Ratchadamnoen Road from Tha Phae Gate. It is listed as open on Sunday evenings, approximately 17:00–24:00, so you can browse the craft and food stalls along the street during those hours while visiting the Old City.
The Tourism Authority also mentions outdoor massage tents along the street. They provide a place to pause during an evening of browsing food and craft stalls.

accessSections.title: Start from Tha Phae Gate
paragraphs: The market runs along Ratchadamnoen Road from Tha Phae Gate towards Wat Phra Singh. Starting at Tha Phae Gate, walk into the Old City to find craft and food stalls along the route.

faq: Where is Sunday Walking Street held?
It runs along Ratchadamnoen Road in Chiang Mai’s Old City, from Tha Phae Gate towards Wat Phra Singh. It is listed as open on Sunday evenings, approximately 17:00–24:00.
Is it the same as Wua Lai Saturday Market?
No. Sunday Walking Street is on Ratchadamnoen Road on Sundays; Wua Lai Market is on Wua Lai Road, south of Chiang Mai Gate, on Saturdays.
What can I eat at the market?
Listed options include khai pam, egg cooked in a banana-leaf cup; mango salad with crispy fish, peanuts and herbs; fried wontons; and fruit and herbal drinks.

wualai-saturday-market.title: Wualai Saturday Walking Street: Crafts and Food in Chiang Mai | ThaiLiveNow
wualai-saturday-market.description: The Wua Lai Saturday Market opens on Saturday evenings on a silversmithing street south of Chiang Mai Gate. Silver jewellery and shops selling lacquerware and textiles sit alongside stalls serving grilled fish and Thai food.
intro: The Wua Lai Saturday Market opens on Saturday evenings on the silversmithing street south of Chiang Mai Gate. Alongside the street’s silversmiths, stalls selling lacquerware, sculpture, textiles and household pieces join the food vendors, bringing Chiang Mai crafts made from different materials together on one street.

Browse silver jewellery and textiles woven by hill-tribe communities, then have grilled fish or pad Thai for dinner. The permanent silver shops on weekdays and the Saturday evening market stalls offer different street scenes.

experiences.title: Crafts in different materials on a silversmithing street
paragraphs: Wua Lai is a street south of Chiang Mai where silversmiths still have shops. At the Saturday market, you can see lacquerware, sculptures, lamps, silk and textiles as well as silver jewellery.

Bags, fabric and household pieces woven by hill-tribe communities are also featured. Silver, lacquer, wood and fabric come together along the street, so you can compare items made from different materials and techniques from one shop to another.

experiences.title: Choose dinner from the food stalls
paragraphs: Choose from grilled fish, som tam, pad Thai or satay with peanut sauce. Coconut sweets and fruit smoothies are also available for a light treat after dinner.

experiences.title: The silversmith shops and Saturday stalls make different plans
paragraphs: The silversmith shops are permanent, but the market stalls selling crafts and food fill the street on Saturday evenings. Visiting during the day to look at the silver shops feels different from coming to the Saturday market for dinner at the stalls.
The Sunday Ratchadamnoen Market is in a different location. If you plan to visit both of Chiang Mai’s walking streets, go to Wua Lai on Saturday and the other market on its Sunday route.

accessSections.title: Find it from Chiang Mai Gate
paragraphs: The Wua Lai Saturday Market takes place on Wua Lai Road, south of Chiang Mai Gate. On Saturday evenings, stalls selling crafts and food line the street with its silversmiths.

faq: When is the Wua Lai Saturday Market open?

It is listed as open on Saturdays, approximately 17:00–22:00. The Wua Lai street with its silversmith shops is there on other days, but that is different from the Saturday market with its food and craft stalls.
Is it the same market as the Sunday Walking Street?
No. Wua Lai Market is on Wua Lai Road, south of Chiang Mai Gate, on Saturdays. The Sunday Walking Street is along Ratchadamnoen Road from Tha Phae Gate on Sundays.
What can I see besides silver goods?
The market features lacquerware, sculptures, lamps, silk and textiles, and bags and fabric woven by hill-tribe communities. Food stalls also serve grilled fish, som tam, satay and coconut sweets.

chiang-mai-night-bazaar.title: Chiang Mai Night Bazaar: Shopping and Dining on Chang Khlan Road | ThaiLiveNow
chiang-mai-night-bazaar.description: The Chiang Mai Night Bazaar is an evening shopping area along Chang Khlan Road. Browse clothing, traditional crafts and souvenirs, then continue to nearby restaurants or the food area at Anusarn Market.
intro: The Chiang Mai Night Bazaar is an evening shopping district where shops open around Chang Khlan Road. Browse clothing, traditional crafts and souvenirs, then have a meal at a nearby restaurant or café.

Unlike the Saturday Wua Lai and Sunday Ratchadamnoen walking streets, the Night Bazaar is listed as open every day. Anusarn Market’s food area and Kalare Night Bazaar are also nearby, but they are separate places. Walk along Chang Khlan Road, then continue to whichever area suits you.

experiences.title: An evening shopping district along Chang Khlan Road
paragraphs: Shops selling clothing, traditional crafts and souvenirs line Chang Khlan Road. Nearby hotels, cafés and restaurants give you places to eat before or after browsing.

Wua Lai on Saturday and Ratchadamnoen on Sunday are walking-street markets that take place on set days. Chang Khlan is open every evening, so the day you can visit depends on which Chiang Mai night market you have in mind.

experiences.title: An evening to browse crafts and clothing
paragraphs: Traditional crafts, clothing and souvenirs are at the centre of the shopping area. Some sellers also go to other weekend markets, but you should not assume that the same stalls and products from Chang Khlan will be available there.

If you want a meal after browsing, head to a restaurant around Chang Khlan or towards the food area at Anusarn Market. Anusarn, with its food area, is a neighbouring market distinct from the Night Bazaar.

experiences.title: Continue your walk to Anusarn Market
paragraphs: Anusarn Market has an area selling food. The Tourism Authority says you can continue about 100 metres farther to shop at Kalare Night Bazaar. You can visit Chang Khlan’s Night Bazaar, Anusarn and Kalare in one walk, but they are separate places.

The approximate 16:00–23:30 hours listed for the Chang Khlan shopping area are not shared opening hours for every nearby market or restaurant. If you have a particular restaurant in mind, follow its own opening hours.

faq: Is the Night Bazaar open only on weekends?

The Night Bazaar along Chang Khlan Road is listed as open daily, approximately 16:00–23:30. Wua Lai on Saturday and Ratchadamnoen on Sunday are separate markets held on set days along different streets.
Is Anusarn Market part of the Night Bazaar?
Anusarn is a separate market close to the Chang Khlan shopping area, with a food section. The Tourism Authority says you can continue about 100 metres farther to shop at Kalare Night Bazaar.

lard-yai-sunday-market.title: Lard Yai Walking Street: Phuket Old Town Sunday Market | ThaiLiveNow
lard-yai-sunday-market.description: Lard Yai Sunday Market opens on Thalang Road in Phuket Old Town on Sundays. Choose batik and crocheted goods in front of the Sino-Portuguese shophouses, and try hor mok and grilled food.
intro: Lard Yai Sunday Market is held on Thalang Road in Phuket Old Town on Sunday evenings. Stalls selling batik, crocheted dolls and crafts, and street food line the Sino-Portuguese shophouses, bringing the old buildings and evening market together on one street.

Admire the façades and signs, then have hor mok or grilled food for dinner and look for a batik bag or a small crocheted item. You can visit the Old Town on other days, but the market stalls are there on Sundays.

experiences.title: A Sunday market in front of Thalang Road shophouses
paragraphs: On Sundays, stalls appear in front of the Sino-Portuguese shophouses on Thalang Road. The market began as a community initiative to preserve local culture, bringing an old shopping street and a present-day street market together in one place.
Walk past the building façades and signs, then choose food or goods from the stalls right outside. The contrast between the regular Old Town street and the Sunday evening market is clearest here.

experiences.title: Batik and crocheted goods
paragraphs: Stalls sell batik fabric and bags, crocheted dolls, hats and jewellery. If you are looking for a small gift, look at the fabric patterns and handmade items.

Behind the stalls are Sino-Portuguese shophouses that you can see on other days too. As you browse handmade goods, the façades and signs remain in view, showing how the Sunday market takes place on a historic Old Town street.

experiences.title: Dinner with hor mok and grilled food
paragraphs: Listed food includes hor mok fish custard, grilled squid, chicken and pork, and pad Thai. After dinner, look for juice, ice cream and Thai sweets.

Street-food stalls line the old shophouses on Thalang Road. Unlike eating in one of the Old Town’s regular restaurants, on Sunday evenings you can carry your chosen food along the street market between the buildings.

accessSections.title: Find the market on Thalang Road
paragraphs: The Sunday market is on Thalang Road in Phuket Old Town, not throughout the entire Old Town. Look for Lard Yai Walking Street to reach the stalls in front of the historic shophouses.

faq: Does Lard Yai Market take place throughout Phuket Old Town?
No. The Sunday market is on Thalang Road in the Old Town. You can explore the historic buildings and shops in the neighbourhood on other days too.
When is it open and what does it sell?
It is listed as open on Sundays from 16:00 to 22:00. You can browse batik fabric and bags, crocheted dolls, hats and jewellery, and try food such as hor mok, grilled dishes, pad Thai and Thai sweets.

cicada-market.description: Cicada Market in Hua Hin is a weekend arts market for creators’ crafts, artworks at ArtFactory, food and an outdoor stage. It opens from 16:00 on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays.
intro: Cicada Market in Hua Hin is a weekend arts market combining creators’ crafts, original artworks, food and music spaces. It offers more than clothing and household goods: you can also see the makers’ designs and exhibits.
Browse home décor and jewellery, see works at ArtFactory, then eat in the garden-style food area. Sasi Open Air Theatre is under a large tree, but its programme changes by date.

experiences.title: A section for creators’ goods
paragraphs: The handmade and ideas section has home décor, clothing, jewellery and souvenirs made by creators. You can see how the items are used and designed, and get a sense of each maker’s style.

If you are looking for a small item for your home or a travel gift, browse the different materials and designs among the clothing, jewellery and home décor. Beyond the creators’ goods section, there is also a space to view artworks.

experiences.title: Original artworks at ArtFactory
paragraphs: ArtFactory is a section for exhibiting and selling original artworks. Unlike the area for browsing crafts, it is a place to take your time looking at paintings and other works.

experiences.title: A garden food area and outdoor stage
paragraphs: The food area is arranged like a garden, with Thai dishes and food from several countries. Sasi Open Air Theatre, beneath a large tree, is an outdoor stage for music programmes.
Different music programmes take place at Sasi Open Air Theatre on different dates. Even when there is no performance, the crafts, artworks and food areas each offer something to browse.

faq: What kinds of things can I see at Cicada Market?

You can browse home décor, clothing, jewellery and souvenirs made by creators, as well as original artworks at ArtFactory. It is a market for design goods and artworks rather than everyday food ingredients.
Are there food and performances?

There is a garden-style food area with Thai dishes and menus from several countries, as well as Sasi Open Air Theatre beneath a large tree. The performance and its timing depend on the date you visit.
When is it open?
The market is listed as opening from 16:00 on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays. You can browse the crafts and artworks and visit the food area in the evening.

grand-palace.thai: พระบรมมหาราชวัง

grand-palace.description: Explore Bangkok’s Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew together. See the Emerald Buddha and royal architecture, and visit the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles, which is included with the same ticket.
intro: Bangkok’s Grand Palace is a complex where you can visit royal halls and Wat Phra Kaew, home of the Emerald Buddha. The grounds bring together different forms of architecture and art, from golden buildings and Ramakien murals to Chakri Maha Prasat, a European-style building topped with a Thai roof.

If this is your first visit to a Thai royal palace and temple, look closely at the golden roofs, murals and hall decorations. The Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles is included with admission too. Some buildings remain in use for royal ceremonies, so not every interior is open to visitors.
facts: **500 baht** · Includes Wat Phra Kaew and the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles
Available from one month before your visit
200 baht separately · Passport or credit card required

experiences.title: Chakri Maha Prasat, a Thai roof over a European-style building
paragraphs: One building to look for at the Grand Palace is **Chakri Maha Prasat Hall**. Its pointed Thai palace roof sits above European-style windows and columns. Look at the arched windows and decorative columns below, then up at the three-tiered Thai roof.

Commissioned by Rama V, the hall is used for royal ceremonies. You can see its exterior, but the throne room and other interiors are not always open to the public. Focus on the roof, windows and column details outside rather than expecting all the rooms to be accessible.

experiences.title: Ramakien murals among the gilded buildings
paragraphs: The cloisters around Wat Phra Kaew feature murals of the Thai epic **Ramakien**. Princes, monkey armies and giants fill the story, with small figures, palaces, forests and battle scenes densely painted across the walls.

After visiting the Emerald Buddha and golden buildings, walk along the mural gallery too. Look closely for small expressions, clothing details and scenes of forests and palaces. Along with the architecture, the paintings offer a look at a traditional Thai story.

experiences.title: One ticket includes the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles
paragraphs: The 500-baht foreign-visitor ticket includes entry to Wat Phra Kaew and the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles. Decide whether you want to see only the temple or include the museum in your visit.

**An audio guide costs 200 baht extra** and requires a passport or credit card as a deposit. Korean is not offered; available languages are English, French, German, Spanish, Russian, Japanese, Mandarin Chinese and Thai.

experiences.title: Royal clothing at the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles
paragraphs: At the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles inside the palace grounds, see royal garments displayed rather than only the clothing shown on the buildings outside. Galleries 3 and 4, ‘Royal Court Textiles of Siam’, feature clothing worn at coronations and other royal textiles. **The exhibition is listed from 30 July 2024 through 30 April 2027.**

Admission to the museum is included in the Grand Palace ticket, so no separate ticket is needed. Plan for its separate hours: **09:00–16:30, last admission at 15:30**. **Photography is not allowed in the galleries**; large strollers, backpacks and umbrellas must be left outside. It is a good addition if you are curious about royal clothing after seeing the palace buildings.

rules.title: Dress appropriately before you set out
paragraphs: Clothing such as **sleeveless tops, short tops, see-through clothing, shorts and miniskirts** is not allowed. Torn trousers, tight-fitting trousers and pyjamas are also restricted. Wear a top that covers your shoulders and long bottoms.

rules.title: Online tickets cannot be changed or refunded
paragraphs: Online tickets **cannot be refunded or changed to a different date or time**. Buy after your travel plans are set and check your visit date once more before paying. Tickets for the day can also be purchased at the on-site ticket office.

rules.title: Follow day-of entrance and access instructions
paragraphs: Visitors enter the Grand Palace through **Mani Noppharat Gate**. Follow on-site directions if the entrance or viewing areas change for royal events or other reasons. Drones may not be flown over the palace.

accessSections.title: Go to the visitor entrance
paragraphs: Search for **The Grand Palace** on a map and go to the visitor entrance, **Mani Noppharat Gate**. If travelling by boat, Tha Chang Pier is an access option. A map pin may point to the centre of the complex, so show the entrance name as well if you arrive by car.

faq: Do I need separate tickets for the Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew?
No. The 500-baht ticket for foreign visitors includes the Grand Palace grounds, Wat Phra Kaew and the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles. They are covered by the same ticket.
Is an English-language audio guide available at the Grand Palace?

Yes. Audio guides are available in English, French, German, Spanish, Russian, Japanese, Mandarin Chinese and Thai; Korean is not listed. Rental costs 200 baht in addition to admission, and you need to leave a passport or credit card as a deposit.
Can I enter the Grand Palace wearing shorts?
Entry is restricted for shorts, miniskirts, sleeveless or short tops, sheer clothing, ripped trousers, tight trousers and pyjamas. Wear a top that covers your shoulders and long bottoms.
Can I enter every building in the Grand Palace?

No. Some halls are still used for royal ceremonies, so not every interior is open. You can see the exterior of Chakri Maha Prasat, including its European-style windows and columns and Thai roof. The ticket also includes royal clothing displays at the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles.

museum-siam.title: Museum Siam Bangkok: Thai Culture Exhibitions and Visitor Guide | ThaiLiveNow
museum-siam.description: Museum Siam in Bangkok explores Thai culture through food, clothing, architecture and everyday objects. Find out about the 14-room permanent exhibition, interactive displays, admission and the route from Sanam Chai MRT Station.
intro: Museum Siam explores Thai culture through food, clothing, architecture and everyday objects. Rather than listing royal artefacts or archaeological collections, it uses everyday things and stories to ask where the ideas we associate with being Thai come from.

Visit after exploring the Grand Palace if you would like to see an indoor exhibition, or if you are curious about the Thai food and daily life you have encountered on your trip. Some displays invite you to handle objects or take part in games, giving you another way to explore beyond reading the explanations. The museum is accessible from Exit 1 of Sanam Chai MRT Station and is closed on Mondays.

experiences.title: Thai identity through food, clothing and architecture
paragraphs: The permanent exhibition, ‘Decoding Thainess’, explores how the idea of being ‘Thai’ has changed over time through history, architecture, traditions, food and clothing. Across 14 galleries, you can see everyday objects from the past and present and read the stories behind them.

If visiting temples and palaces has made you curious about what people ate, wore and how they lived, take time to explore this exhibition. Look for the stories that connect the clothes and food you have seen on the streets with the displays here.

experiences.title: Culture through everyday objects and hands-on activities
paragraphs: The gallery on traditions and festivals is arranged like a storeroom. Explanations and pictures inside the boxes, along with objects you can handle and games, introduce customs and traditions in an interactive way.

In the photo gallery, choose clothes, accessories, a backdrop and props, then take a picture. You can move from reading about an exhibit to choosing objects and joining in, making this a good visit with friends or family who enjoy hands-on displays.

experiences.title: Stop by Muse Shop and the restaurant after your visit
paragraphs: Muse Shop stocks history books and museum-themed stationery, jewellery and household items. In its small DIY area, you can make a souvenir yourself. After exploring Thai daily life in the galleries, it is a nice place to browse books and small keepsakes.

There is also a restaurant and café inside the museum for a meal or coffee after your visit. You can use an audio guide in the galleries and leave your bags in a locker. If you need a wheelchair, ask the information desk about borrowing one and the accessible route.

rules.title: Choose the ticket that matches your free or student admission
paragraphs: General admission is **100 baht for Thai and international visitors alike**. **Thai and international visitors under 15 and visitors aged 60 or older enter free**; students aged 15 and above pay 50 baht. Bring proof of student status if you are applying for the student fare. Ask the ticket office which ticket applies to the documents you have.

rules.title: Audio guides and lockers are available
paragraphs: The museum provides **audio guides, wheelchairs and lockers**. You can listen to exhibition information or leave your belongings in a locker while you explore.

accessSections.title: Arrive from Sanam Chai MRT Station
paragraphs: If you are travelling by rail, use **Exit 1 at Sanam Chai Station on the MRT Blue Line**. Search for Museum Siam on a map.

faq: Is Museum Siam suitable for children?

There are displays where visitors can handle everyday objects, play games and take photos with selected costumes, props and backdrops. Foreign visitors under 15 enter free; students aged 15 and over need proof of student status to receive the student discount.
Is Museum Siam open on Mondays?
The museum is closed on Mondays. It is open Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 18:00.
Which station should I use for Museum Siam?
Take the MRT Blue Line to Sanam Chai station and leave through Exit 1. The destination is Museum Siam.

national-museum-bangkok.name: National Museum Bangkok

national-museum-bangkok.title: National Museum Bangkok: Art, History and Visitor Information | ThaiLiveNow
national-museum-bangkok.description: Explore Thai history, archaeology and art in the former Front Palace buildings and later exhibition halls at National Museum Bangkok. See Buddhist art, traditional crafts and royal funeral chariots in one visit.
intro: National Museum Bangkok presents Thai history, archaeology and art in the former Front Palace buildings and later exhibition halls. Its collections include Buddhist art, traditional crafts and royal funeral chariots.

Visit if you are curious about the different styles of Buddha images you have seen in temples, or would like to look more closely at Thai royal crafts. Explore several exhibition halls, from small sculptures and crafts to large funeral chariots. The museum is closed on Mondays, Tuesdays and public holidays, so plan your visit on another day.

experiences.title: Buddhist art and royal crafts in one place
paragraphs: The collection starts with prehistoric artefacts and continues through the art of Thailand’s different kingdoms to the present Chakri dynasty. Religious artworks include pieces from the late 6th century onwards, letting you see objects from different periods together rather than only images at one temple.

Alongside Buddha images, the museum displays traditional crafts associated with the royal court. If you have seen large Buddha images and halls at temples, here you can look closely at sculpture and craft objects and examine their materials and decoration. Visitors interested in religious art and royal life can explore both kinds of collection in the same visit.

experiences.title: A grand carriage used for royal funerals
paragraphs: You can also see **large, elaborate carriages used for royal funerals.** After viewing small objects in cases, the size of the carriages stands out when you approach them. Up close, take a look at the decorations covering their surfaces.

Compare small craft objects with a huge ceremonial carriage in the same museum. If you are interested in Thai royal ceremonies and traditional crafts, look at the carriage’s decorations one by one as well as its size.

experiences.title: The Si Hin Buddha and murals in a former palace chapel
paragraphs: The museum’s historic buildings are not new galleries made to resemble part of a palace; they are buildings from the former Front Palace where the viceroy lived. Built in 1782, the Front Palace became a museum in 1887, and the present museum also includes exhibition buildings added later.

In the chapel housing the Si Hin Buddha, look at the walls behind and beside the image. Murals depicting the Buddha’s life remain on the interior walls. Unlike viewing objects in cases, here you can experience the whole worship space inside the building, with the Buddha image and murals together.

rules.title: Free guided tour starts at the ticket office at 09:30
paragraphs: **The National Museum Volunteers’ regular tours in October 2026 depart from the museum ticket office at 09:30.** The tour is free; museum admission is charged separately. You can join a regular tour without booking in advance.

In October 2026, regular tours in English, French and Japanese run on Wednesdays and Thursdays; German tours run on Wednesdays. There are additional Saturday tours in English on 3 October and French on 24 and 31 October. **This schedule is for October 2026** and the same days are not guaranteed in other months.

accessSections.title: Walk from Tha Chang Pier
paragraphs: The Tourism Authority of Thailand lists the museum as about a **15-minute walk from Tha Chang Pier**. Set your destination to National Museum Bangkok on Na Phrathat Road.

faq: Are guided tours available in English?
Yes. In October 2026, NMV lists on-site tours in English, French, German and Japanese. A Korean PDF visitor guide is also available, but it is not an audio tour or an on-site Korean-language guide.
Are the in-person guided tours free?

The National Museum Volunteers’ regular tours are free, while the museum admission fee of 240 baht is separate. For October 2026, the schedule lists a 09:30 meeting time at the ticket office on the stated days, with no advance booking required. See the schedule above for the tour days by language.
What can I see at Bangkok National Museum?

In the former Front Palace buildings, you can see prehistoric artefacts, Buddhist art, royal crafts and royal funeral carriages. The Buddhaisawan Chapel has the Phra Si Hin Buddha and murals depicting the Buddha’s life.
When is Bangkok National Museum closed?
The museum is listed as closed on Mondays, Tuesdays and public holidays. Visiting ends at 16:00.

jim-thompson-house.thai: พิพิธภัณฑ์บ้านจิม ทอมป์สัน
jim-thompson-house.type: Museum in a former home with an art collection
jim-thompson-house.title: Jim Thompson House Museum Bangkok: Guided Tour and Visitor Guide | ThaiLiveNow
jim-thompson-house.description: Visit the teak houses and Asian art collection at Jim Thompson House Museum in Bangkok. Find details about guided tours of the main house, admission and children’s fares, and how to get there from Exit 1 at BTS National Stadium.
intro: Jim Thompson House Museum lets you visit the home of Thai silk entrepreneur Jim Thompson and the Asian art he collected. Six teak houses stand in a garden beside a canal in central Bangkok. It suits visitors who want to see traditional Thai house architecture and historic artworks close up amid the shopping malls and tall buildings around Siam.

You visit the main house with a guide who explains the building and collection. This is different from a shop where you browse silk products. Visit with a friend who enjoys architecture or art, or add a historic house to your Bangkok itinerary. See the wooden houses together with the garden around them.
jim-thompson-house.addressKo: 6 Kasem San 2 Alley, Rama I Road, Wang Mai, Pathum Wan, Bangkok

experiences.title: Six teak houses moved to Bangkok
paragraphs: Jim Thompson bought old houses from different parts of Thailand and moved them to Bangkok. The houses were dismantled and transported, then reassembled by carpenters from Ayutthaya and joined into one residence of six houses. Work began in 1958 and was completed the following year. Thompson lived here himself.
Across the canal in front of the house is Ban Krua, a weaving community. A garden surrounds the wooden houses, so alongside the art indoors, you can also see the garden and views around the canal.

experiences.title: Asian artworks collected by a silk entrepreneur
paragraphs: Jim Thompson was a silk entrepreneur, an art collector and someone who studied architecture. In the late 1950s, he collected Asian art and antiques and decided to build a house to hold his collection. Here you can see the wooden houses where he lived together with the artworks displayed inside.

The same complex also has an art centre and other exhibitions and shops. These are separate spaces from the main museum house, and a ticket to the main house does not necessarily include entry to every other exhibition in the complex.

experiences.title: From Buddha images to blue-and-white and Benjarong ceramics
paragraphs: The collection includes Buddhist sculpture, Thai paintings, blue-and-white ceramics from China and Annam, and Benjarong ceramics made for the Thai royal family. You can view artworks from different periods and regions in one place.

Benjarong ceramics include bowls painted with flowers and animals in several colours, while blue-and-white ceramics have blue patterns on a white ground. If you are interested in the collection, you can preview images and descriptions through the foundation’s online exhibition.

faq: Can I visit Jim Thompson House without booking in advance?

Yes. You can visit by buying a ticket on site without booking in advance. The museum says same-day on-site admission operates even when online bookings are sold out. To buy online, use the ticket seller linked from the Admission page on the museum’s website.
Are guided visits available in English?
Yes. The museum lists guided visits in Thai, English, French, Chinese and Japanese; Korean is not listed. Visits to the main house are accompanied by a guide.
Can I take photographs inside Jim Thompson House?

Photography inside the main house is allowed, but flash, selfies, personal portraits and video recording are prohibited. Remove your shoes before entering; bags larger than 20 cm must be left in a locker.
Can I visit the main house with a pushchair or wheelchair?
The main house is a wooden structure with several staircases and no lift. It is difficult to move through the entire main house with a pushchair or wheelchair.

ancient-city-muang-boran.name: Muang Boran (Ancient City)
ancient-city-muang-boran.thai: เมืองโบราณ
ancient-city-muang-boran.title: Muang Boran (Ancient City): Architecture and Visitor Guide | ThaiLiveNow
ancient-city-muang-boran.description: Muang Boran is a large outdoor museum in Samut Prakan, with recreated architecture and displays from across Thailand. Despite its name, not every building is an ancient ruin preserved in its original location.
intro: Muang Boran is an outdoor museum in Samut Prakan where you can see palace and temple architecture from different parts of Thailand in one place. Some buildings to explore inside and out include Sanphet Prasat, a reconstruction of the lost Ayutthaya palace, and Dusit Maha Prasat, recreated with reference to historical records.

Visit with friends or family who enjoy photographing and comparing the roofs, doors and windows of palaces and temples. Unlike historic cities where ruins remain in their original locations, this museum also includes reconstructed buildings that no longer survive. If you have visited the remains of the palace in Ayutthaya, you can also see here how a palace has been recreated from historical records.

experiences.title: Sanphet Prasat, recreating the lost Ayutthaya palace
paragraphs: Sanphet Prasat recreates the central hall of the Ayutthaya royal palace. The original palace burned during the fall of Ayutthaya, leaving only its base. At Muang Boran, researchers studied the remains and historical records to recreate the architecture and interior decorations.

The **tiered roof, pointed spire and mother-of-pearl doors and windows** draw on several historical sources. Inside are gold-coloured columns, mirror decorations and murals depicting stories of Vishnu’s incarnations. After photographing the whole building, take a closer look at the smaller details on its doors and windows.

experiences.title: Dusit Maha Prasat, informed by research into an early palace
paragraphs: Dusit Maha Prasat is not a direct copy of the Grand Palace building in Bangkok today. Researchers studied old photographs and documents to recreate an earlier form, and independent columns that had been removed from the original palace hall were installed again in the interior here. Look at the cross-shaped building and high roof, then go inside to see how the columns support the roof.

The columns’ colours and patterns refer to the base of Wat Pho’s Reclining Buddha in Bangkok, while the murals between the windows draw on paintings at Wat Nang Nong in Thonburi. They depict royal ceremonies and religious, military and diplomatic events, as well as Thai life. If you have already seen the Grand Palace in Bangkok, look here at the recreated early structure and its interior decorations.

experiences.title: An open-air museum comparing regional architecture
paragraphs: Palaces and temples from northern, northeastern, central and southern Thailand are arranged in areas representing different regions. You can compare regional architecture in one place instead of travelling between cities across Thailand.

Choose the architecture you want to see on the map first. For a group visit, you can choose a golf cart; if you prefer to pedal, you can hire a bicycle. If you bring your own car into the park, the vehicle entry fee for foreign visitors is **400 baht per vehicle.**

At Ayutthaya’s palace site, you see the remains that still stand; here, you see a palace reconstructed from historical records. It is not the palace in its original location, but an exhibit that helps visitors picture what the palace might have looked like when only its base remained.

rules.title: Vehicle entry fee and golf-cart driving conditions
paragraphs: The fee to bring your own car into the park is separate from golf-cart rental. **For international visitors, vehicle entry costs 400 baht per car and does not include the driver’s admission.**

To drive a golf cart yourself, you must be **at least 18 and hold a Thai or international driving licence**. If you are visiting with older adults or anyone who finds long walks difficult, consider a golf cart as a way for your group to get around together.

faq: Are the old ruins at Muang Boran in their original locations?

Muang Boran is an open-air museum recreating architecture and sites from different parts of Thailand in one place. Some buildings differ from the remains at the original site, such as Sanphet Prasat, which recreates the lost Ayutthaya palace, and Dusit Maha Prasat, which represents an earlier form.
Can I drive a golf cart myself?
Drivers must be at least 18 and have a Thai driving licence or an international driving permit. Golf carts are a separate mode of transport from admission.
Can I bring my own car into Muang Boran?
The vehicle entry fee is 400 baht per car. The driver’s admission is not included in this fee.
How much is admission for children at Muang Boran?
Admission for foreign children aged 6–14 is 400 baht; admission for foreign adults is 800 baht.

erawan-museum.description: At Erawan Museum in Samut Prakan, see the enormous three-headed elephant building, its three levels of exhibits and the surrounding garden. The museum includes interior galleries as well as the sculpture outside.
intro: Erawan Museum in Samut Prakan is known for its enormous building topped by a three-headed elephant. After viewing the sculpture outside, go indoors to explore three levels: antiques and ceramics below, a stained-glass ceiling and religious decoration, then Buddha images and a celestial ceiling painting inside the elephant.

It suits visitors who want to photograph unusual architecture or enjoy Thai religious art and ceramics. There are small decorative details to see inside as well as the large sculpture outside, and after the museum you can walk around the garden with its mythical-animal figures. The museum is operated in connection with Muang Boran, but the two are separate facilities in different locations.
facts: 250 baht · Check applicable age and height when purchasing

experiences.title: Antiquities and Benjarong ceramics in the Suvarnabhumi Basement
paragraphs: The Suvarnabhumi Basement displays old objects and ceramics collected by the museum’s founder, Lek. Among the smaller pieces are Benjarong ceramics decorated in several colours, offering a different experience from the grand exterior of the building.

The displays are arranged across three realms: the underworld, the human world and heaven. After seeing the enormous elephant sculpture outside, you can go inside and explore the collection in the basement before continuing upstairs to the religious decoration.

experiences.title: A stained-glass ceiling that depicts the four elements
paragraphs: Inside the circular building supported by the elephant is a **stained-glass ceiling**. Yellow, white, red and blue represent earth, air, fire and water, with zodiac imagery around the edge. After admiring the elephant from outside, step in and look up at the ceiling.

The pillars supporting the elephant’s four legs tell stories from different religions: the Buddhist Jataka tales, Vishnu, Guanyin, and the Christian stories of creation and Jesus. Small decorative pieces around the stairs use pottery fragments made in Amphawa and China. After looking up, take a closer look at the figures and patterns on the pillars and railings.

experiences.title: Inside the elephant, the atmosphere changes
paragraphs: The heavenly realm is an exhibition space built **inside the elephant’s body**. A Buddha footprint and a Sukhothai-style Buddha image stand at the centre, with other Buddha images along the walls. The ceiling depicts the sun, planets, the Milky Way and asteroids, creating a cosmic scene unlike the stained glass below.

From the old objects in the basement, pass through the level representing the human world and arrive at the heavenly realm with its cosmic imagery. The exhibits and lighting change as you move between levels. Outside, the garden has sculptures of mythical creatures and is a pleasant walk after seeing the interiors.

experiences.title: A garden of creatures from Thai mythology
paragraphs: The surrounding garden features trees from Thai literature and sculptures of mythical creatures, making it worth a walk after the indoor galleries. Garden admission, flowers, incense and lotus flowers are included with the ticket. Audio guides are available in Korean as well.

rules.title: Use the lift in the elephant’s left leg to reach the celestial level
paragraphs: The route to the celestial level inside the elephant’s body is divided between an **elevator in the left leg** and **stairs in the right leg**.

faq: Can visitors go inside the elephant at Erawan Museum?

Yes. The three-headed elephant contains an exhibition space representing heaven. You can see a Buddha footprint, a Sukhothai Buddha image and a ceiling depicting the cosmos; the lower level has the collection, stained glass and pottery-fragment decorations.
Is there a lift to the exhibition inside the elephant?
There is a lift inside the elephant’s left leg and stairs inside its right leg. Both lead to the heavenly-realm exhibition inside the elephant.
Is an English audio guide available at Erawan Museum?
Yes. Audio guides are available in Korean, Thai, English, Chinese and Russian.
Are Erawan Museum and Muang Boran the same place?

No. They are separate attractions run by the same organisation. Erawan Museum presents a collection, religious art and a garden inside and around the giant elephant sculpture. Muang Boran is a large open-air museum recreating architecture from across Thailand.

ayutthaya-historical-park.description: Ayutthaya Historical Park spans the former royal capital, with palace remains and temple ruins at several locations. It is not one enclosed park where every site can be reached on foot from a single entrance.
intro: Ayutthaya Historical Park lets you explore palace remains and temple ruins in Siam’s former capital. Founded around 1350, the city grew into a centre of international trade and diplomacy before it was destroyed in the war of 1767. Its chedis and the remains of halls still tell that story.

Each site has a different character: Wat Mahathat is known for a Buddha head embraced by tree roots, Wat Phra Si Sanphet has three chedis in a row, and Wat Chaiwatthanaram stands beside the river. It suits visitors interested in history and architecture, or those who want to see both Bangkok’s Grand Palace and the former capital. The ruins are scattered through the modern city rather than enclosed within one park.
facts: Visit separate ruins · admission and travel are handled site by site

experiences.title: Traces of Ayutthaya, an international trading city
paragraphs: Ayutthaya was founded around 1350 and became the capital of Siam after Sukhothai. Surrounded by three rivers, it grew into a centre of trade and diplomacy, but **the old city was destroyed in the war of 1767 and remains as ruins.**

The main sights are therefore not lavishly furnished palace interiors, but tall towers, collapsed halls and large temple grounds. As you look at the scale of the surviving buildings, imagine how large the former capital was. The old city of Ayutthaya is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

experiences.title: A Buddha head in tree roots, three chedis and a riverside temple
paragraphs: To see a Buddha head wrapped in tree roots, visit Wat Mahathat; for three chedis standing in a row and a royal temple site, choose Wat Phra Si Sanphet. If you want a central prang and surrounding galleries beside the river, consider Wat Chaiwatthanaram.

Wat Phra Si Sanphet is a royal temple connected with the palace grounds, while Wat Chaiwatthanaram stands by the river, where its towers and galleries form part of the waterside scene. Rather than stopping after a photo of one Buddha image, visit a royal temple and a riverside temple to compare the different scale and layouts of Ayutthaya’s surviving religious architecture.

experiences.title: Palaces, temples and the present-day city
paragraphs: Ruins are spread throughout the present-day city. Choose the sites you want to visit and allow time to travel between them.
Some temples are still active places of worship, while others remain as ruins. Clothing, fees and entry arrangements are not the same at every site.

experiences.title: Choose a pass based on the ruins you plan to visit
paragraphs: Even a combined pass does not provide entry to every temple and museum in Ayutthaya. Wat Mahathat, with the Buddha head among tree roots; Wat Phra Si Sanphet, with its royal chedis; and riverside Wat Chaiwatthanaram are separate sites that require travel between them. A combined pass has its own list of included sites and validity period.

rules.title: Each site has different visiting hours
paragraphs: The historical park is spread across multiple sites, so **opening hours and last admission vary by location.** One site opening at night does not mean the entire historical park remains open into the evening.

faq: Is Ayutthaya Historical Park all in one place?
The ruins are spread across several temples and palace sites in and around the city. It is not a single enclosed park where you enter and see everything; you travel between the different sites.
Where is the Buddha head in the tree roots?
It is at Wat Mahathat. Wat Phra Si Sanphet, where three royal chedis remain, and riverside Wat Chaiwatthanaram are separate sites.
Why are there so many ruined temples in Ayutthaya?
Ayutthaya was the capital of a kingdom founded around 1350, but it was destroyed in the war of 1767. The historical park’s surviving chedis, walls and palace grounds show traces of the old capital.

sukhothai-historical-park.description: Sukhothai Historical Park has temples, chedis and Buddha images inside and outside the old city walls. Plan for separate central, northern and western zones, as their locations and tickets differ.
intro: Sukhothai Historical Park lets you explore temples, chedis and Buddha images inside and outside the walls of the old city. See Sukhothai architecture and Buddhist sculpture up close, from Wat Mahathat’s lotus-bud-shaped chedi to the large seated Phra Achana Buddha at Wat Si Chum.

It suits visitors who want to walk among historic temples and take in the architecture and scenery. The central, northern and western ruins are in separate zones with different tickets. Exploring several temples in the central zone offers a different experience from visiting the large Buddha beyond the city walls.
facts: 400 baht · check included zones and validity when buying

experiences.title: A lotus-bud chedi and a large seated Buddha
paragraphs: Wat Mahathat in the Central Zone was an important temple of the Sukhothai Kingdom. The central **lotus-bud-shaped chedi** is its signature structure. Buddha images and hall foundations remain nearby, so explore the surrounding remains after seeing the main chedi.

Outside the city walls, Wat Si Chum houses a large seated Buddha called Phra Achana. After visiting the temples in the Central Zone, travel beyond the walls to see the image up close. This is a good visit if you are interested in Sukhothai Buddhist sculpture as well as temples and chedis.

experiences.title: Walk among the remains of the old city
paragraphs: Sukhothai’s heritage extends beyond one temple. Temples and chedis are scattered inside and outside the old city walls, forming a UNESCO World Heritage property together with the historic towns of Si Satchanalai and Kamphaeng Phet. Which ruins you see depends on their location: Wat Si Sawai and Wat Sa Si are inside the walls, while Wat Si Chum is outside.

Within the walls, you can explore several temples, including Wat Si Sawai and Wat Sa Si, on foot or by bicycle. Allow extra travel time for remains outside the walls. Instead of rushing through every zone, choose the temples you want to see and enjoy their architecture and surroundings.

experiences.title: Zone tickets and Saturday night lighting
paragraphs: According to the Tourism Authority’s August 2026 information, the Central Zone costs 200 baht, the North and West zones 120 baht each, and a full ticket 400 baht. The ruins are spread inside and outside the walls, so a Central Zone visit covers a different area from a ticket for additional zones.

Lighting is listed until 21:00 on Saturdays. Check the same-day guidance for the zone you intend to visit, as it does not follow that every ruin and ticket office offers the same night-entry conditions.

experiences.title: Wat Si Sawai, with three remaining towers
paragraphs: If you are exploring inside the walls, include Wat Si Sawai. Its three towers stand side by side and look different from the lotus-bud chedi of Wat Mahathat in the Central Zone. Up close, notice the pointed Khmer-style towers and their decoration.

The three towers preserve a history that runs from Hindu architectural influence to a Buddhist temple. Rather than thinking of Sukhothai as having a single architectural style, compare the towers at Wat Mahathat and Wat Si Sawai. Wat Si Chum, in the North Zone, is a different part of the park.

rules.title: Wat Si Chum is in the North Zone
paragraphs: The large seated Phra Achana Buddha is at **Wat Si Chum in the North Zone**. A Central Zone ticket does not cover every other zone.

rules.title: A tram is another option for visitors who find walking difficult
paragraphs: If it is difficult to walk between the ruins, you can take the **park tram for 60 baht per person**. The Tourism Authority lists departures about every 15 minutes. The tram fare is separate from the Central Zone admission ticket.

If you prefer to set your own pace, you can rent a bicycle. K-Shop on the east side lists a rate of **30 baht per day, paid afterward**. This is K-Shop’s price; other rental businesses may charge differently.

faq: Can I rent a bicycle near the east entrance to Sukhothai Historical Park?
K-Shop on the east side lists bicycle rental at 30 baht per day, paid afterward. Its stated hours are 05:30–19:00; this price applies to that shop.
Is there a way to see the ruins without walking?
The park tram is listed at 60 baht per person, with departures about every 15 minutes. Admission to the ruins is separate from the tram fare.
Is Wat Si Chum, with its large seated Buddha, in the Central Zone?

No. Wat Si Chum, with its Phra Achana Buddha, is in the North Zone. Wat Mahathat, with its lotus-bud chedi, and Wat Si Sawai, with three towers, are inside the walls in the Central Zone. Central, North and West are separate zones with separate admission.
