phimai-historical-park.description: Phimai Historical Park preserves a Khmer stone temple in Phimai, northeast of Nakhon Ratchasima. See Buddhist and Hindu carvings, layered petal-like roof details and the temple courtyard together.
intro: Phimai Historical Park is a place to see a Khmer stone temple in Nakhon Ratchasima, in northeastern Thailand. Walk from a bridge guarded by a seven-headed naga through gateways and galleries to the central sandstone sanctuary.

Look for carved Buddhas and Hindu deities, petal-like roof ornaments and a courtyard with ponds. The stone colours and carvings offer a different experience from temples with extensive gold decoration. Phimai was connected by a route to the old Khmer capital of Angkor, making it a compelling stop for anyone interested in Khmer-era temples in Thailand.

experiences.title: Get close to stone Buddhas and Hindu deities
paragraphs: Phimai’s appeal lies not only in the broad outline of its Khmer stone sanctuary but also in the carvings that remain in the stone. **Sculptures of Buddhas and Hindu deities** appear together, showing how Buddhist and Hindu imagery was expressed in temple architecture.

The colours and materials differ from Bangkok’s richly gilded temples. After walking around the towers, look near the doorways for smaller figures and patterns carved into the stone. If you enjoy stone architecture, take your time with the surfaces and carvings.

experiences.title: A religious site once connected to Angkor
paragraphs: Routes from Phimai once linked to Angkor, the capital of the old Khmer Empire. Although the area is now divided between Thailand and Cambodia, religion and culture travelled along these routes in the past.

The courtyard has four ponds, and layered roof decorations resemble overlapping flower petals. After seeing the central tower, explore the courtyard and doorways. This is not a newly built replica modelled on Angkor Wat; it is a temple with remains from the old Khmer period.

experiences.title: A bridge guarded by a seven-headed naga
paragraphs: At the southern entrance stands a sandstone bridge carved with a **seven-headed naga**. Its long body forms the balustrade, with the heads spreading out at the end. As you pass through the gateway, also look at the balustrades and the lion sculptures beneath the stairs.

The naga bridge is interpreted in Buddhist and Hindu cosmology as a path linking the human world with heaven. Religious meaning is built into the approach to the temple too. Walk from the bridge towards the central tower and notice the carvings on the balustrades, gateway and steps.

experiences.title: A restored site assembled from old stonework
paragraphs: The central sanctuary is built of pale sandstone, while red stone towers and galleries remain in the surrounding area. Compare the colours and surfaces of the different structures and see how the doorways and galleries frame the central sanctuary.

What you see today combines ancient remains and modern restoration. In the 1960s, the Thai Fine Arts Department worked with France to restore the central sanctuary by matching scattered architectural pieces to their original positions. This is a researched and conserved historic site, not a newly made themed building.

accessSections.title: Travel from Korat to Phimai Historical Park
paragraphs: Set your destination to **Phimai Historical Park, Nai Mueang, Phimai**. It is described as about 59 km from central Korat, so arrange separate transport for the return journey as well.

faq: Is Phimai Historical Park in central Korat?
No. It is in Phimai, about 59 km from central Korat. Allow separate travel time there and back rather than treating it as a stop in central Korat.
What can I see at Phimai?

See the southern bridge with its seven-headed naga, sandstone towers and steps with lion sculptures. Compare the pale central tower with the red towers to notice differences in material and decoration.
Is Phimai a newly built replica?
No. It is a restored Khmer historic site. During joint Thai–French restoration in the 1960s, surviving architectural pieces were reassembled.

intro: Phanom Rung Historical Park is a Khmer temple complex on an ancient volcanic hill in Buriram. Follow the long stone walkway and steps through its gateways and stone architecture; from the upper area, you can also look out over the surrounding fields.

It suits visitors who want to climb past a stone temple and take in the fields below. The site is also known for sunlight passing through all 15 doorways in a line. This does not happen every day, but on an ordinary visit you can still walk the long approach and see the doorways and sanctuary aligned in perspective. If anyone in your group has difficulty with steps, ask in advance which routes are available.
facts: 150 baht combined ticket with Muang Tam ruins listed

experiences.title: Khmer architecture on an ancient volcanic hill
paragraphs: Phanom Rung means ‘large hill’ in Khmer. It is a **temple built on an ancient volcano**, first associated with Hinduism and later also with Buddhism. Follow the long stone causeway and steps through the gateways to reach the temple high above.

The approach is part of the visit: you pass along the causeway and steps and through the gateways before reaching the buildings. With stone architecture and views of the surrounding fields, it suits visitors who enjoy walking through historic architecture and landscapes rather than only viewing indoor artefacts.

experiences.title: A line of doorways aligned with the sunlight
paragraphs: Phanom Rung has **15 doorways arranged in a straight line**. When the sun’s direction aligns with their orientation, sunlight passes through them. Even when the alignment is not visible, you can see the doorways framed one behind another along the passage.

The special light effect depends on the date, weather and access conditions. For a regular visit, focus on the old stone temple and hilltop scenery. If seeing the alignment is essential, plan around an announcement for the event dates in the year you intend to visit.

experiences.title: Pass the five-headed naga bridge on the way to the temple
paragraphs: Along the long processional path are sandstone pillars shaped like lotus buds. At the end of the route, the naga bridge has a **serpent-shaped balustrade with five heads**. Naga are understood as beings connecting the human world with heaven, giving the approach a religious significance as well.

Phanom Rung was dedicated to Shiva, and the central tower on the hill represents Mount Kailash, where the god lives. Follow the processional path, bridge and steps to the tower to see how the temple’s layout uses the hillside.

experiences.title: Stories of Shiva and Vishnu carved above the doors
paragraphs: The central sanctuary is made of pink sandstone. Above the doorways, look for a pediment with Shiva dancing and the **Narai Banthomsin lintel** depicting Vishnu reclining on a naga. Look closely at the figures and decoration above the doors as well as the sunlight alignment.

The Vishnu lintel was taken abroad and **returned in 1988 before being reinstalled at Phanom Rung**. It is not newly made themed decoration, but a stone artefact removed from the temple and later returned. The present appearance of the temple also reflects restoration work that studied and reassembled the old stonework.

rules.title: The approach includes stone paths and steps
paragraphs: The temple is on a hill and reaching it **involves walking up a stone causeway and steps**. The usual visitor route is not a flat stroll and may be difficult for anyone who has trouble with stairs.

faq: Can I see sunlight passing through Phanom Rung’s doorways every day?
No. It is an alignment effect associated with the 15 doorways, visible at particular times. Weather and access conditions also affect what you can see.
Is there a combined ticket for Phanom Rung and Muang Tam?
The listed admission is 100 baht for Phanom Rung alone or 150 baht for a ticket including Muang Tam.
Are there many steps at Phanom Rung?
The temple is on an ancient volcanic hill, and the usual visitor route includes a long stone causeway and steps. You walk uphill, cross the naga bridge and continue to the central sanctuary.

siam-amazing-park.description: Siam Amazing Park combines amusement rides and water attractions in Bangkok. The rides area and water park have different hours, so plan your order if you want to visit both.
intro: Siam Amazing Park is a place to enjoy rides and water attractions on the same day in Bangkok. Water World has a large wave pool, a lazy river and fast slides, while the rides range from the Vortex roller coaster to smaller attractions for children.

Ride a roller coaster with friends who enjoy fast attractions, or spend time at the smaller rides and pools with children. If you plan to do both, arrange your day around the different opening hours of the two areas. Tickets also differ in which areas they include.

experiences.title: A day at the wave pool or on fast slides
paragraphs: Water World has a **large wave pool**. Play in the pool as artificial waves roll in, or float along the Flowing Pool on a tube. It is an option if you want water activities in Bangkok without travelling to the sea.

For fast rides, try the Speed Slide or Super Spiral. With young children, explore the family water-play area with Siam Lagoon and mini slides. **Some areas require children to be accompanied by an adult**, so check the ride entrance before allowing a child to go on alone.

experiences.title: Water activities and roller coasters in one visit
paragraphs: This attraction has rides as well as a water park. On Vortex, ride through turns in a seat where your feet hang free; Giant Drop offers a drop from a height. If your group likes fast rides, you can spend more time in this area.

With young children, look for Small World, with mini boats and a small carousel. Decide whether you want the water park alone or rides as well, then choose a ticket covering the areas you plan to visit.

experiences.title: Browse food and architecture at Bangkok World outside the park
paragraphs: Outside the park, **Bangkok World** has recreated Bangkok-style old buildings, food and craft shops. Browse regional products and handmade goods from around Thailand and find something to eat.

These are not original buildings preserved in Bangkok’s old town; they are recreations inspired by historic architecture. Bangkok World is a separate area outside the water park, with architecture and shops rather than water attractions. It is an option for group members who prefer to see the buildings or enjoy food instead of fast rides.

experiences.title: Choose water activities and smaller rides by height
paragraphs: The Water World Speed Slide and Super Spiral require visitors to be **at least 121 cm tall**. Children must be accompanied by an adult in the wave pool, Siam Lagoon, Flowing Pool and mini-slide areas. A child ticket does not allow a child below the height limit to ride a slide.

Small World’s mini motorcycle, mini boat, Playport and mini Astro Fighter are **for children 101–130 cm tall**. The mini carousel is for children up to 130 cm; children 100 cm or shorter must ride with an adult. If siblings are different heights, use these limits to check which rides they can enjoy together.

rules.title: Outside food and drinks are not allowed
paragraphs: **You cannot bring outside food or drinks into the park.** Leave them out when packing for the water park. You can store your belongings in one of the paid lockers listed below.

rules.title: You need your ticket and a hand stamp to re-enter
paragraphs: The operator says re-entry is allowed with a **valid ticket and a hand stamp**. If you plan to leave the park temporarily, get the re-entry mark before you go out.

rules.title: Height and health restrictions vary by ride
paragraphs: Entry to the park does not mean every ride is suitable for you. Follow the **height, weight, health and accompanying-adult requirements** posted at each attraction.

faq: Can I use the water park until 18:00?
The park is open 10:00–18:00, but Water World closes at 17:00. The rides area and water park have different closing times.
Can I bring outside food and drinks?
Bringing outside food or drinks is prohibited.
Can I leave the park and come back in?
Re-entry requires a valid admission ticket and a hand stamp.
Are there rides for young children?

Small World has mini boats, mini motorcycles, Playport and Astro Fighter rides for children 101–130 cm tall. The mini carousel is for children up to 130 cm, and children 100 cm or shorter need to ride with an adult. The Water World Speed Slide and Super Spiral require a height of at least 121 cm.

dream-world.description: Dream World is an amusement park in Pathum Thani, north of Bangkok. It has rides and separate attractions such as Snow Town, and the experiences included depend on the ticket you choose.
intro: Dream World is an amusement park in Pathum Thani, north of Bangkok. Alongside rides such as Sky Coaster and Viking, you can visit Snow Town for indoor sledding below zero, or see photo spots inspired by a giant’s house and storybook settings.

Ride coasters and spinning attractions with friends, or enjoy photo spots and snow play with children. You can spend the day moving between rides and storybook-inspired photo settings. Keep in mind that admission-only tickets cover different things from packages that include rides and Snow Town.

experiences.title: Choose rides for children and friends by height
paragraphs: Black Hole Coaster requires a height of **at least 121 cm**; Sky Coaster and Super Splash require **at least 130 cm**. Viking, Hurricane and Tornado require **at least 140 cm**, while Go-Kart requires **at least 155 cm**. If your group includes people of different heights, a shared ticket does not mean everyone can ride the same attractions.

There are rides for smaller children too. The Mouse Coaster, Flying Fish and Space Train are listed for visitors **at least 90 cm tall**. Your group can split up between larger coasters and children’s rides, then meet at places such as the cable car or Giant’s House. Follow each ride’s adult-accompaniment and health restrictions, as well as the day’s safety instructions.

experiences.title: Snow Town, with an indoor sledding slope
paragraphs: Snow Town is a below-zero indoor attraction with a **large sledding slope** and snowy scenery. After enjoying outdoor rides in the heat, you can come inside to play in the snow. It is another activity for children who are too small for the coasters.

A Snow Town ticket costs **190 baht for one entry** and includes a jacket, boots and socks. Not every admission ticket includes Snow Town; park entry, rides and Snow Town are covered differently by each package. A Trip.com Super Visa product name alone does not establish that Snow Town is included.

experiences.title: Photos at Giant’s House and storybook settings
paragraphs: The park also has **Giant’s House and a cable car**, Love Garden and Photopia. At Photopia, take pictures with settings such as an upside-down castle, a hobbit house and a fairytale princess castle. These are places for the whole group to enjoy together, including anyone who skips fast rides.
The ‘Colours of the World’ parade is also listed for weekends. Unlike the photo settings, it is not a daily show, so include it in your itinerary if you are visiting on a weekend and want to see it.

rules.title: Discounts have eligibility and ticket limits
paragraphs: Ticket products differ in **whether foreign visitors are eligible and whether admission, rides and Snow Town are included**. Promotions based on Thai card-member points, for example, apply only to customers who meet those eligibility requirements.

faq: Does Snow Town cost extra at Dream World?
A separate Snow Town ticket costs 190 baht for one entry and includes a jacket, boots and socks. Not every admission ticket includes Snow Town; package inclusions vary.
Does Dream World have a parade every day?
Colours of the World is listed as a weekend programme, not a daily event.
Can children ride every attraction at Dream World?

No. Rides have different height limits. Mouse Coaster, Flying Fish and Space Train start at 90 cm; Black Hole at 121 cm; Sky Coaster and Super Splash at 130 cm; Viking, Hurricane and Tornado at 140 cm; and Go-Kart at 155 cm. Health and adult-accompaniment rules also apply by ride.

andamanda-phuket.description: Andamanda Phuket is a water park themed around Thai mythology and the Andaman region. Its wave pool, slides and children’s areas make it a day out for families and friends.
intro: Andamanda Phuket is a water park themed around Thai mythology and the Andaman region. Enjoy different kinds of water play across the wave pool, slides and children’s areas, whether you are visiting with family or friends.

Try the fast slides with friends or spend time with your family in the children’s areas. The Village is themed around a Thai market, while Tropical Beach serves seafood, giving you places to stop for a meal and a break.

experiences.title: Water attractions inspired by Thai myths and Andaman scenery
paragraphs: Andamanda takes its themes from Thai mythology, Phuket’s Sino-Portuguese architecture and the Andaman region’s limestone scenery. Move between the wave pool, slides and children’s areas to enjoy the water and the park’s themed details.

Plan a day in the children’s areas with family or ride slides with friends. Each attraction has its own height, weight and health restrictions, so check the conditions at the entrance of the rides you intend to use.

experiences.title: Andaman scenery around the wave pool and island features
paragraphs: Andaman Bay has a wave pool and a sandy beach area, along with a feature shaped like Koh Tapu. You can enjoy water activities **in a park setting inspired by Andaman limestone islands** without travelling to an actual island.

For fast rides, look for the capsule-style Dragon’s Drop, whose floor opens, or Eagle Flyer, which climbs and descends along a wall. Racing Nagas lets friends start side by side. The rides have different movements, so choose the one that suits you.

experiences.title: Water-play areas for children
paragraphs: Little Reef has small slides, while Wonder Waterland has a splash-play structure. At Atoll Adventure, **a large bucket dumps water** over the play area. These are options for children who are not ready for the larger slides.

Rolling Ripples is a tube ride along a flowing course, and there are also raft-style rides for families. Height, weight and adult-accompaniment requirements differ between the children’s areas and large slides, so park admission does not mean everyone can ride every attraction together.

experiences.title: A market-inspired restaurant and pool bar between swims
paragraphs: The Village is designed like a Thai market and serves Thai and Western food. You can also find mango sticky rice, crepes and cut seasonal fruit for a meal or snack between swims. Plan to eat inside the park rather than bringing food in.

Adult groups can order drinks at Wave Bar, beside the infinity pool. Families can use the Coral World dining area, then head back to the rides after a meal. Check the park map for The Village, Coral World and the wave pool to plan between meals and water activities.

rules.title: Children must not be left unattended
paragraphs: **Do not leave children unattended.** The park **strongly recommends an adult accompany visitors under 18**. This is the general park recommendation; follow any mandatory adult-accompaniment conditions posted at individual rides.

rules.title: Limits on food and cameras
paragraphs: **Outside food and drinks are prohibited.** Handheld cameras may not be used on rides, and photography is prohibited in restrooms and changing areas.

rules.title: Operations may pause in severe weather
paragraphs: Pools and rides may temporarily stop during severe weather. Follow the safety staff’s instructions about operations and waiting.

rules.title: Bring suitable swimwear and rental items
paragraphs: Wear appropriate swimwear; clothing with metal decorations or zippers may be restricted on rides. Children who need nappies must wear swim nappies.
It is advisable to store valuables in a rented locker. If your booking includes towels, lockers or a shuttle, check the inclusions so you do not pack or book them twice.

faq: Are children’s tickets at Andamanda based on height?
Yes. Adults are listed as 122 cm and above, children as 91–121 cm, and the senior category as age 60 and over. Individual slides have separate height, weight and health restrictions.
How much does it cost to rent towels and lockers?
Towels and lockers are each listed at 200 baht online or 250 baht on site.
Can I bring food or drinks into Andamanda?
Outside food and drinks are prohibited. The park has dining options, including Thai and Western food and desserts at The Village and seafood at Tropical Beach.
Can I take photos while riding the slides?
No. Handheld cameras may not be used on rides. Photography is also prohibited in restrooms and changing rooms.

ramayana-water-park.description: Ramayana Water Park, south of Pattaya, has slides and pools for adults and children. Plan a visit around both thrill rides and water play with children.
intro: Ramayana Water Park, south of Pattaya, has a range of slides and pools. Choose from attractions with different levels of intensity, such as the Aqua Coaster with its rising and falling tube, the trapdoor Freefall, a children’s splash area and a lazy river.

Ride in a shared tube with friends or race side by side on the Mat Racer. Families with children can centre their visit on the children’s areas and pools. You can also take a break on the sun loungers provided between rides.
facts: Visitors **under 15 must be accompanied by an adult**

experiences.title: Ride together on tubes or try a trapdoor slide
paragraphs: If you want to ride with friends, choose attractions such as Aquacoaster, where the tube moves up and down, or Python and Aquaconda, which take large tubes through twists and enclosed passages. **Matt Racer** lets riders start side by side in parallel lanes.

For a stronger drop, try a different type of ride such as Freefall, with a trapdoor, or the looping Aqualoop. Slides have different height, weight and health conditions; meeting the park-entry requirements on an affiliate ticket does not automatically qualify you for an individual ride.

experiences.title: From children’s splash areas to the lazy river
paragraphs: Hanuman’s Splash has several slides and a water-play structure with a large tipping bucket. Mermaid Lagoon and Lanka Town are areas for young children. If a child is not ready for fast rides, enjoy these play areas together.

**Float through caves and water jets on the lazy river.** In the wave pool, play as the waves roll in. You could spend part of the day on slides with friends and another part in a pool or children’s area with family.

experiences.title: A day of slides and pools
paragraphs: A standard admission ticket allows use of the slides and pools during opening hours. Sunbeds, tubes, mats and life jackets are also available. Tubes and life jackets are first come, first served, so your preferred size may not be available immediately.
Children under 15 must be accompanied by a responsible adult. Rules for using children’s flotation aids in pools differ from the rules for bringing them onto adult slides.

experiences.title: Wristband payments and rental items
paragraphs: Bars and stalls inside the park primarily accept cashless payment using the QR on your wristband. Add credit at a designated location and refund any remaining balance at a shop before leaving.

**Towels cost 150 baht each**; lockers are **169 baht for medium and 259 baht for large**. Tubes and life jackets are free and first come, first served. If you want the remaining wristband balance refunded, do so before the shop’s 17:45 refund deadline.

experiences.title: Operations and compensation in rainy weather
paragraphs: Rain alone does not automatically qualify for a refund. Compensation depends on the time the safety team officially suspends pool and ride operations continuously.

If pools and rides are suspended for **more than two consecutive hours, you may receive a 50% discount voucher for a future visit**; after **more than three consecutive hours, you may receive a future admission ticket**. Each is valid for six months after issue. **These are not cash refunds**, and separate suspensions are not added together if operations resume in between.

experiences.title: Check both height and weight for larger slides
paragraphs: Matt Racer requires a height of **at least 106 cm and a maximum weight of 135 kg**. Freefall and the looping Aqualoop have stricter limits: **at least 122 cm and 45–135 kg**. Meeting the park’s entry requirements does not automatically qualify you for these rides.

For young children, look for Lanka Town or Mermaid Lagoon. Lanka Town is **a play area for children aged 1–4 with a parent**, with gentle slides. Mermaid Lagoon has wide slides for parents and children to ride together and softer flooring, giving smaller children another way to enjoy the water.

rules.title: A new ticket is required to re-enter
paragraphs: One ticket covers one entry and exit. **If you leave, you need a new ticket to re-enter**, so bring everything you need with you.

rules.title: Outside food is allowed only by exception
paragraphs: Outside food and drinks are generally prohibited. Exceptions listed include **baby food and special diets supported by medical documentation**.

rules.title: Follow camera rules for each ride
paragraphs: Cameras cannot be used on body slides. Tube slides have conditions for action cameras secured with a designated strap, and **selfie sticks are prohibited on all rides**.

faq: Can children under 15 enter without an adult?
Children under 15 must enter with an adult. Each slide also has its own height and weight conditions, separate from the children’s areas.
Can I bring outside food?
Outside food is prohibited, with exceptions for baby food and special diets supported by medical documentation.
Can I leave Ramayana and re-enter?
Re-entry requires a new admission ticket.
Will I get a refund if rides stop because of rain?

The policy is not a cash refund. Official guidance says a continuous weather-related suspension of more than two hours may qualify for a 50% discount on a future visit; more than three consecutive hours may qualify for a future admission voucher. Each is valid for six months, and separate suspension periods are not combined.

columbia-pictures-aquaverse.description: Columbia Pictures Aquaverse in Chonburi is a water park themed around movie characters and scenes. Enjoy areas inspired by Hotel Transylvania, Jumanji and Ghostbusters, among others.
intro: Columbia Pictures Aquaverse in Chonburi is a water park themed around movie characters and scenes. Explore areas inspired by Hotel Transylvania, Jumanji and Ghostbusters while enjoying the water attractions.

If you like Ghostbusters, Jumanji or Hotel Transylvania, enjoy water attractions in areas inspired by scenes from the films. Ride slides with friends or explore character-themed splash areas with children. Go-karts and mini golf are also available, but whether they are included depends on the ticket product.

experiences.title: Ghostbusters ghost-hunting as a water ride
paragraphs: In the Ghostbusters area, **Proton Stream** takes riders on a raft into the Stay Puft water dome. Ghost Trap Adventure is a fast water coaster, while Slimer Speed Racer is a set of parallel tube slides. Look for favourite characters while trying different kinds of ride.
It is fun to spot the ghost-hunting gear and characters around the area. If you are visiting with a film fan, compare how the names and ideas from the movie have been turned into water attractions.

experiences.title: Jumanji’s jungle and Hotel Transylvania’s splash area
paragraphs: The Jumanji area has **Viper, Jungle Stampede and Jaguar Mountain**. Hotel Transylvania is an aqua-play area with several slides and water-play structures, a place for families who enjoy the film characters.
A child’s ticket does not mean every ride in the area is suitable. Follow the **height and adult-accompaniment requirements** posted for each attraction, even in themed areas.

experiences.title: Spend time in the lazy river and wave pool
paragraphs: Swallow Falls lazy river takes riders on tubes through a setting themed around the food-filled imaginary world from the film. There is also a large wave pool and an outdoor performance space, so you can take a break from fast slides for other water activities.
Shows and events are sometimes held on the outdoor stage. The schedule varies by date, so the same performance is not available every day.

experiences.title: Go-karts and mini golf as separate activities
paragraphs: At the Gran Turismo Racing Club, ride go-karts themed around the film and game. Emoji Mini Golf offers a round with character backdrops. They are options for groups who want activities beyond the water park.
**Whether go-karts and mini golf are included depends on the ticket you choose.** The park is closed on Wednesdays, and the affiliate product described above is also unavailable on Wednesdays.

rules.title: Ticket inclusions and ride requirements differ
paragraphs: **Tickets differ in whether they include water attractions, go-karts and mini golf.** A child ticket does not permit every ride; each attraction has its own rider requirements.

faq: Is Aquaverse open on Wednesdays?
It is listed as closed on Wednesdays. Visiting hours on operating days are 10:00–18:00.
Are go-karts and mini golf included with Aquaverse admission?
Gran Turismo go-karts and Emoji Mini Golf are activities separate from the water attractions, and inclusions vary by package. They are not included with every ticket.
Can I take an Aquaverse shuttle from Pattaya?
An online round-trip fare for the Pattaya city shuttle is listed from 300 baht. It is separate from park admission.

intro: Vana Nava Water Jungle is a jungle-themed water park in Nong Kae, Hua Hin. Its attractions include a lazy river that passes trees, caves and bridges, children’s splash areas, and adult slides such as the Abyss, which drops into a giant funnel, and Boomerango, which climbs a wall.

Play among fountains and small slides with children, or share a large tube on a fast ride with friends. The park also has a surf simulator, ropes and climbing facilities, so you can combine water attractions with other activities. Conditions vary by attraction, and not every activity is included with every admission ticket.
facts: 1,400 baht listed for visitors at least 122 cm tall
1,000 baht listed for children 111–121 cm tall
1,000 baht listed for visitors aged 60 and over

experiences.title: A lazy river and family splash areas among the jungle
paragraphs: Float along the lazy river on a tube, following the waterway **between trees, caves, bridges and islands.** Unlike a slide that sends you down quickly in one go, this is a ride where you travel with the current and take in the surroundings.

Kiddie Cove has fountains, play structures and children’s slides. Rain Fortress has water-play structures and several slides, and there is also a children’s area called Vana Wonderland. If you are visiting with young children, these areas offer places to play in the water beyond the larger slides.

experiences.title: The Abyss funnel and Boomerango’s wall ride
paragraphs: **The Abyss is a slide for up to six riders on one tube.** The official description says it starts 28 metres up, passes through a near-vertical turn and enters a large funnel. Unlike a body slide ridden alone, the group faces one another on the same tube as it turns and drops.

Boomerango is a tube ride that climbs a high wall before coming back down. Its motion is different from The Abyss, which enters a funnel, so the two rides offer different experiences. Six is the maximum number of people on The Abyss tube; each rider must also meet the ride’s height, weight and health requirements.

experiences.title: Surf and climbing activities that test your balance
paragraphs: The Surf Zone’s **Double FlowRider is an artificial wave machine with fast-flowing water.** Instead of sliding down on a tube, you balance on the moving water. You can try it inside the park without going out to sea.

If you enjoy active challenges, look for the rope course and climbing wall too. Buying a child admission ticket does not mean every attraction is available to that child. Follow the **height, weight and health limits** for each activity.

rules.title: Towels and lockers can be rented separately or included in a package
paragraphs: A towel rental is **100 baht** and a locker is **150 baht**. The online Adult Splash Day Pass includes one towel, one locker and unlimited VR slide access.

The online promotion listed above is **for adults at least 122 cm tall** and is the displayed price for a visit date selected on October 21, 2026. Rental items are not included with every standard ticket.

faq: Are towels and lockers included in the Vana Nava ticket?

Renting only a towel costs 100 baht; renting only a locker costs 150 baht. The Adult Splash Day Pass selected for 21 October 2026 cost 1,200 baht and included admission, one towel, one locker and unlimited VR access. The contents and price of this package are not guaranteed to be the same on other visit dates.
What are the child admission requirements at Vana Nava?
The child rate is 1,000 baht for a height of 111–121 cm; the adult rate is 1,400 baht for a height of 122 cm or more. The senior rate for visitors aged 60 and over is 1,000 baht.
Can families rent a place to rest together?
A cabana costs 1,400 baht per day and fits 6–8 people; a beach hut costs 900 baht per day and fits 2–4. Both have a fan and power supply, and the park assigns the location.

wat-traimit.description: Wat Traimit is the Golden Buddha temple near Bangkok’s Chinatown. The main visit is to the golden seated Buddha in its hall, and you can continue on foot into Yaowarat afterwards.
intro: Wat Traimit is a temple near Bangkok’s Chinatown where you can see the Golden Buddha. Knowing the story that the statue, once concealed beneath plaster, was revealed when it was moved makes the golden image in the hall all the more striking.

Explore the hall housing the Golden Buddha and the large mondop building, then walk to the streets and restaurants of Yaowarat. It makes a good day out for visitors interested in Buddhist art and the story of the statue, with time for a meal and a stroll in Chinatown too.
facts: 100 baht · the history centre is a separate visitor area

experiences.title: A 5.5-tonne golden Buddha revealed when the plaster cracked
paragraphs: The Buddha image is said to have been covered in plaster for a time, hiding its golden surface. The story goes that the plaster cracked while the image was being moved, revealing the gold underneath. The golden Buddha you see today comes with a story about its appearance being uncovered much later.

The seated gold image is described as weighing about 5.5 tonnes. Inside the hall, you can see its face and seated posture; outside, look at the large mondop that houses it. Remembering the discovery story may draw your attention to the golden surface now on display.

experiences.title: See the Golden Buddha and Yaowarat history displays separately
paragraphs: The Golden Buddha’s formal name is Phra Phuttha Maha Suwanna Patimakon. After viewing the seated image in the large mondop, visit the Yaowarat History Centre in the same temple if you are interested in the exhibits. The Tourism Authority of Thailand says they cover several themes in the history of Bangkok’s Chinese community and the development of the neighbourhood.

The Buddha’s worship area and the history-centre exhibits are separate visitor areas. If you want to see both, check on site what your ticket includes. Allow separate time for a visit focused on the Golden Buddha and a walk through Chinatown, and for a visit that also includes the history displays.

experiences.title: Continue from the temple into Yaowarat
paragraphs: The temple is close to the edge of Chinatown. After seeing the architecture and Buddha image during the day, you can continue with a walk among Yaowarat’s shops and restaurants. Set aside time separately for the temple and for a meal in the neighbourhood.

Even if you are mainly interested in Chinatown’s evening atmosphere, the temple visit needs to fit within its daytime viewing hours. Arrive before heading out for dinner so you can see the temple first, then experience both a religious site and the street scene in one neighbourhood.

rules.title: Suggested clothing for a temple visit
paragraphs: For all visitors, we recommend wearing clothing that **covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a good choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

accessSections.title: Getting there from Hua Lamphong MRT station
paragraphs: It is listed as about a 10-minute walk from **Hua Lamphong station (BL28) on the MRT Blue Line**. The destination is Wat Traimit on Mittaphap Thai-China Road.

faq: Was the Golden Buddha always visible as gold?

No. It is said to have been covered in plaster for a time, until the plaster cracked while the image was being moved and the gold underneath was revealed. The hall now houses a golden seated Buddha weighing about 5.5 tonnes.
Are the Yaowarat History Centre and the Golden Buddha in the same exhibit?

They are in the same temple but are separate visitor areas. The Golden Buddha is housed in the large mondop, while the Yaowarat History Centre covers Bangkok’s Chinese community and the development of the neighbourhood. The worship site and local history displays offer different things to see.

wat-benchamabophit.name: Wat Benchamabophit · Marble Temple
wat-benchamabophit.thai: วัดเบญจมบพิตร
wat-benchamabophit.type: Temple with marble architecture and a Buddha-image gallery
wat-benchamabophit.title: Wat Benchamabophit: Bangkok’s Marble Temple and Buddha Gallery | ThaiLiveNow
wat-benchamabophit.description: Wat Benchamabophit is a marble temple in Bangkok’s Dusit district. See the hall built with marble imported from Italy and the gallery lined with Buddha images.
intro: At Wat Benchamabophit, light marble and stained glass sit beneath a Thai-style roof. The temple in Bangkok’s Dusit district is known as the Marble Temple because marble imported from Italy was used in its construction.

After admiring the marble exterior and Thai-style roof, look inside the main hall at the Phra Buddha Chinnarat image and the bronze Buddhas lining the outer gallery. The pale stone, coloured windows, golden Buddha and gallery columns each have a different character, making this a good place to enjoy architecture and Buddhist art together.

experiences.title: Italian marble beneath a Thai-style roof
paragraphs: The temple was designed by Prince Narisara Nuwattiwong during the reign of Rama V. Italian Carrara marble and stained glass were added to traditional Thai architecture, creating light surfaces and colours unlike brick ruins or wooden halls.

From a distance, the symmetrical rooflines and halls stand out first. Up close, look separately at the stone surfaces and windows. Visitors who enjoy architecture can compare traditional building forms with materials brought from Europe in one place.

experiences.title: A bronze replica based on the Phra Buddha Chinnarat
paragraphs: The golden Buddha image in the main hall is a bronze replica based on the Phra Buddha Chinnarat. The original is enshrined at Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat in Phitsanulok. Here in Bangkok, you can see the form of the Chinnarat image through a separately made statue.

Notice the contrast between the blue-toned interior and the golden image behind it. After seeing the light marble outside, step into the main hall to experience the different colours and atmosphere inside.

experiences.title: The outer gallery lined with bronze Buddha images
paragraphs: Bronze Buddha images also line the gallery around the hall. Rather than stopping at the main building, walk around the gallery to see the images and architecture together. The repeated figures between the columns are another feature of the temple.

After seeing the bright marble exterior, continue to the Phra Buddha Chinnarat image in the main hall and the outer gallery. Look closely at the statues, then walk through the gallery and take in the columns and roof. The main hall is listed as open until 17:00, so leave enough time for the interior visit.

rules.title: Suggested clothing for a temple visit
paragraphs: For all visitors, we recommend wearing clothing that **covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a good choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

accessSections.title: Travel by road after taking the BTS
paragraphs: The Tourism Authority describes reaching the temple by road from **Phaya Thai BTS station**. Enter Wat Benchamabophit, Dusit as the destination. The temple is not directly beside the station.

faq: Is the Chinnarat Buddha in the main hall the original from Phitsanulok?
No. The main hall houses a bronze replica modelled on Phra Phuttha Chinnarat. The original is enshrined at Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat in Phitsanulok.
What can I see besides the marble?

After viewing the Thai-style roof and stained glass, look around the Chinnarat Buddha in the main hall and the bronze Buddha images lining the outer gallery. The main hall is listed as open until 17:00, so visit before then if you want to see inside.

wat-suthat.type: Temple with murals, Buddha images and a separate museum
wat-suthat.title: Wat Suthat and the Giant Swing: Murals, Carved Doors and Museum | ThaiLiveNow
wat-suthat.description: Wat Suthat is an old-city Bangkok temple near the Giant Swing. Highlights include the hall murals, carved wooden doors and the Si Sakyamuni Buddha. The large red swing outside is a separate structure.
intro: Wat Suthat is a temple in Bangkok’s old city where you can see the large red Giant Swing outside, murals inside the viharn and finely carved wooden doors. Take in the Sisaakayamuni Buddha image on its high pedestal and the paintings on the walls for a closer look at the temple beyond its street view.

A separately listed museum is open 09:30–16:00 on Friday, Saturday, Sunday and public holidays, with admission at 200 baht. The temple is open 08:30–20:00, with admission at 100 baht. If you want to visit both on the same day, plan around the museum’s limited opening days and earlier closing time.
facts: Friday, Saturday, Sunday and public holidays, 09:30–16:00 · 200 baht

experiences.title: The Sisaakayamuni Buddha on a high pedestal
paragraphs: Sisaakayamuni is a large bronze Buddha image made in the Sukhothai period. The image is about 8 metres tall and sits on a pedestal about 6 metres high. Step into the viharn and look up to appreciate the scale of the image and its base.

After seeing the red Giant Swing outside, enter the viharn to find the Buddha image raised high above you and paintings on the walls. Rather than taking a street-side photo and moving on, set aside time to look up at the large image and take in the murals.

experiences.title: Murals and finely carved wooden doors
paragraphs: The temple was begun in the early 19th century during the reign of Rama I. It is known for its murals and intricately carved wooden doors, so look at both the image and the building’s walls and entrances. Take time to alternate between the large paintings and small carved details.

Near the doors, look at the patterns carved into the wood; inside, explore the scenes depicted across the murals. Even if Buddhist art is unfamiliar, you can follow the delicate lines of the carvings and the images spread across the walls.

experiences.title: The Giant Swing and the temple’s other stories
paragraphs: Sao Ching Cha, the Giant Swing in front of the temple, consists of red posts and a crossbar. The Tourism Authority of Thailand says it was used in a Brahmin ceremony that was discontinued long ago. Do not mistake the historic structure for a ride or an event that is still taking place.

The swing is outside the temple, while the Sisaakayamuni Buddha and 19th-century murals are inside the viharn. Seeing the historic structure associated with an earlier Brahmin ceremony and then entering the temple lets you explore art from different religious traditions and periods. The museum is listed separately as open 09:30–16:00 on Friday, Saturday, Sunday and public holidays, closing before the temple.

rules.title: The temple and museum have different hours
paragraphs: The temple is listed as **08:30–20:00, 100 baht**; the separate museum is **09:30–16:00 on Friday, Saturday, Sunday and public holidays, 200 baht**. If visiting the museum, plan around its earlier closing time.

rules.title: What to wear at the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear clothing that **covers the shoulders and knees**. A top with sleeves and long trousers or a skirt covering the knees are suitable choices. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

accessSections.title: Walk from Sam Yot MRT station
paragraphs: It is listed as about a 10-minute walk from **Sam Yot station (BL30) on the MRT Blue Line**. The destination is Wat Suthat at 146 Bamrungmuang Road.

faq: Is the Giant Swing inside the temple?

The red Giant Swing is outside the temple. It was once used for a Brahmin ceremony, which has since been discontinued. Inside the viharn, you can see the Sisaakayamuni Buddha on a high pedestal, murals and carved wooden doors.
Is the museum open at the same times as the temple?

The temple is listed as open 08:30–20:00 with admission at 100 baht. The museum is separately listed as open 09:30–16:00 on Friday, Saturday, Sunday and public holidays, with admission at 200 baht. The museum opens on fewer days and closes earlier.

wat-paknam.name: Wat Paknam Phasi Charoen
wat-paknam.thai: วัดปากน้ำภาษีเจริญ
wat-paknam.type: Temple with a giant Buddha and an interior chedi ceiling painting
wat-paknam.title: Wat Paknam: Giant Golden Buddha and Chedi Ceiling Art in Bangkok | ThaiLiveNow
wat-paknam.description: Wat Paknam is a royal temple in Bangkok’s Phasi Charoen district. It is known for the large golden Buddha outside and a ceiling painting inside the upper level of the chedi.
intro: Wat Paknam is a royal temple in Phasi Charoen, Bangkok, where the large golden Buddha outside and the ceiling painting on the upper floor of the chedi are in different spaces. First take in the full 69-metre seated Buddha from outside, then go inside the chedi to see the painting of the Buddha’s life.

Founded in the Ayutthaya period, the temple also has a tradition of Pali education for monks and meditation associated with Luang Pho Sot. Sightseeing and meditation programmes are separate activities, so be mindful of practitioners and worshippers as you explore the grounds.

experiences.title: The large golden seated Buddha completed in 2021
paragraphs: The large golden seated Buddha outside the temple was completed in 2021. This bronze image is 69 m tall and sits in a meditative posture. It is large enough to see from around the temple grounds. First take in its overall form from a distance, then move closer to look at its face and seated posture.

From farther away, view the Buddha together with the temple surroundings; up close, take in the seated figure and hall separately. The monumental image outside and the paintings indoors are different highlights in different spaces.

experiences.title: Ceiling paintings depicting the life of the Buddha
paragraphs: On the upper level of the chedi, you can see ceiling paintings depicting the life of the Buddha. After seeing the large golden image outside, go inside and look up at the paintings. You can explore Buddhist art in the temple interior as well as the scale of the Buddha image.

Please be considerate of worship and religious practice while viewing the paintings. Follow on-site information about which upper areas are open. If anyone in your group needs to use stairs or a lift, it may be helpful to ask about the route before your visit.

experiences.title: An Ayutthaya-era temple and a tradition of meditation
paragraphs: Wat Paknam is a royal temple whose history dates to the Ayutthaya period. It is also known for training monks in Pali and the meditation teachings of Phra Mongkhon Thepmuni, known as Luang Pho Sot. The newly built large Buddha stands within a longer history of education and religious practice.

Separate from tourist visits, Dhamma talks and meditation programs are held at Charoen Vipassana Hall. **Meditation and Dhamma talks are free and conducted in Thai.** White clothing is recommended for participants; it is not a requirement for every visitor. If you would like to join, check the schedule and conditions separately.

rules.title: Explore without disturbing worship or meditation
paragraphs: General viewing of the ceiling painting is separate from meditation and Dhamma talks at Charoen Vipassana Hall. Give worshippers space in front of the painting. If you join a meditation session, note its separate conditions: **it is free and conducted in Thai.**

rules.title: What to wear when visiting the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear **clothing that covers the shoulders and knees.** A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a practical choice. Please visit in respectful clothing rather than a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

accessSections.title: Getting there from Bang Phai MRT station
paragraphs: It is listed as about a 12-minute walk from **Bang Phai station (BL33) on the MRT Blue Line**. The destination is Wat Paknam Phasicharoen on Ratchamongkhon Prasat Alley, 300.

faq: Are the large golden Buddha and the ceiling painting in the same place?

No. The 69-metre golden bronze seated Buddha, completed in 2021, is outside, while the painting of the Buddha’s life is inside the upper floor of the chedi. Visit the two spaces separately to see the temple’s scale and Buddhist art.
Do I have to wear white?
White clothing is recommended for people joining meditation or Dhamma talks; it is not an entry requirement for all temple visitors. Sessions at Charoen Vipassana Hall are free and conducted in Thai.

wat-mahathat-ayutthaya.name: Wat Mahathat
wat-mahathat-ayutthaya.thai: วัดมหาธาตุ พระนครศรีอยุธยา
wat-mahathat-ayutthaya.type: Ayutthaya temple ruins with a Buddha head and brick remains
wat-mahathat-ayutthaya.title: Wat Mahathat Ayutthaya: Buddha Head in Tree Roots and Brick Ruins | ThaiLiveNow
wat-mahathat-ayutthaya.description: Wat Mahathat in Ayutthaya is a temple ruin known for a Buddha head embraced by tree roots. The grounds also contain collapsed brick walls, hall foundations and headless Buddha images.
intro: At Wat Mahathat in Ayutthaya, tree roots wrap around the face of a sandstone Buddha image. The image is the site’s best-known feature, but look beyond it and you will find the remains of a large temple, with headless Buddha images, collapsed brick walls and the bases of halls.

Gold Buddha images, jewellery and other artefacts were found during restoration in 1956. You can see the brick ruins and the sandstone Buddha face among the roots here; to see the excavated objects, visit Chao Sam Phraya National Museum separately.

experiences.title: A sandstone Buddha face embraced by tree roots
paragraphs: The Buddha head that represents the temple is made of sandstone. With its body and hall gone, tree roots now wrap around the face. Look closely at the roots extending around it, then step back to see the tree and Buddha image together.

A story says that the sandstone Buddha head fell beneath a tree during a war. Exactly how the roots came to surround the face is not known, but the image and the grown tree now remain together as one scene.

experiences.title: Temple ruins with brick walls and headless Buddha images
paragraphs: The temple is said to have once had a golden chedi top, before it fell into ruin after a war. Today, headless Buddha images, hall floors and collapsed walls remain. Though the buildings are no longer intact, you can follow the statue locations and remaining foundations to imagine the scale of the old temple.

After photographing the Buddha head, look at the direction of the brickwork and where the images stand. Even without roofs and walls, the foundations and arrangement of sculptures show traces of a former religious complex. The site may appeal to visitors interested in old architecture and history.

experiences.title: Gold artefacts found beneath the ruins
paragraphs: Gold Buddha images, jewellery and other artefacts were found during restoration in 1956. The excavated objects are listed as being displayed at Chao Sam Phraya National Museum. Their discovery shows that there was once a space beneath the visible brick ruins where valuable objects were kept.

At Wat Mahathat, explore the temple grounds and architecture; visit Chao Sam Phraya National Museum separately to see the excavated objects. If you plan to visit several ruins, check which sites are included and how long a pass remains valid when you buy it on site. Older prices for a combined pass may differ from the current terms.

rules.title: A Wat Mahathat ticket and an Ayutthaya ruins pass cover different sites
paragraphs: The **individual admission fee for Wat Mahathat is listed as 80 baht.** A separate pass for several Ayutthaya ruins has its own list of included sites and validity period. A Wat Mahathat ticket alone does not provide entry to other temples.

rules.title: What to wear when visiting the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear **clothing that covers the shoulders and knees.** A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a practical choice. Please visit in respectful clothing rather than a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

faq: How did the Buddha head become surrounded by tree roots?
A story says that the sandstone Buddha head fell beneath a tree during a war. Its exact path to its current position has not been established; today, the roots surround the face.
Can I see the gold objects excavated here?

At the ruins, you can see the Buddha head among the roots and the remains of the brick temple. Gold Buddha images, jewellery and other objects found during restoration in 1956 are listed as being displayed at Chao Sam Phraya National Museum.

wat-phra-si-sanphet.name: Wat Phra Si Sanphet
wat-phra-si-sanphet.thai: วัดพระศรีสรรเพชญ์
wat-phra-si-sanphet.type: Royal temple ruins in the former Ayutthaya palace
wat-phra-si-sanphet.title: Wat Phra Si Sanphet: Three Royal Chedis in Ayutthaya | ThaiLiveNow
wat-phra-si-sanphet.description: Wat Phra Si Sanphet was the royal temple connected to Ayutthaya’s former palace. Its three aligned chedis and the remaining building foundations give a sense of the temple’s scale within the old royal palace.
intro: At Wat Phra Si Sanphet, three large bell-shaped chedis stand in an east–west line. This royal temple was connected to the former palace of Ayutthaya. Walk among the surviving chedis and hall foundations to appreciate the scale of a place where royal ceremonies took place.

Each chedi enshrines the remains of an Ayutthaya king. The extensive foundations of halls used for royal ceremonies also remain, reflecting a temple built for royal remembrance and religious rites. After viewing the three aligned towers, follow the foundations to see where the halls once stood.

experiences.title: Three chedis for three kings
paragraphs: The eastern, central and western chedis each enshrine the remains of a king: Borommatrailokkanat, Borommarachathirat III and Ramathibodi II. The three bell-shaped towers stand side by side as memorials to the kings.

From a distance, take in the arrangement of the three structures; up close, look at each rounded body and its rising spire. The Fine Arts Department explains that smaller surrounding chedis also enshrine members of the royal family.

experiences.title: From former royal palace to royal ceremonial site
paragraphs: This site was originally a royal palace. After King Borommatrailokkanat moved the palace north, the former palace grounds became a temple used for royal religious and state ceremonies. An oath of allegiance to the king and royal family was also held here.

The halls and palace buildings are not all intact today. Look at the foundations and the direction of the towers to picture the layout of the temple beside the palace. This is a site from a different dynasty and city from Wat Phra Kaew at the present-day Bangkok Grand Palace.

experiences.title: The lost golden standing Buddha and its story at Wat Pho
paragraphs: The royal hall once housed a standing Buddha covered in gold, Phra Si Sanphet. The Fine Arts Department explains that when Ayutthaya fell, the gold was stripped away and the bronze core remained; King Rama I later moved it to Bangkok’s Wat Pho, where it was enshrined inside a chedi.

There is no large golden Buddha remaining at the hall foundations today. Picture the former hall as you look at the place where the image was enshrined and the building base. If you also visit Wat Pho in Bangkok, you can see the chedi where the damaged statue was re-enshrined. The history of the same Buddha connects the two cities.

rules.title: The 2026 event pass is different from a regular visit
paragraphs: The Fine Arts Department’s event information for 2026 lists Phra Si Sanphet and the palace as one item on an event pass. The event hours are not the regular opening hours, and the event pass should not be treated as an ordinary admission ticket. Visiting the old palace grounds is limited to areas open to the public.

rules.title: What to wear when visiting the temple
paragraphs: Visitors of all genders are advised to wear **clothing that covers the shoulders and knees.** A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a practical choice. Please visit in respectful clothing rather than a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

faq: What were the three chedis built for?

The bell-shaped chedis to the east, centre and west house the remains of King Borommatrailokanat, King Borommarachathirat III and King Ramathibodi II, respectively. The three large towers show that this was a royal memorial site.
Is the old golden standing Buddha still at the temple?

No. The Fine Arts Department explains that after Ayutthaya fell and the gold was stripped away, Rama I moved the remaining bronze image to Wat Pho in Bangkok and enshrined it inside a chedi. The palace ruins and chedis remain at this site.

wat-chaiwatthanaram.type: Khmer-style temple ruins beside the river
wat-chaiwatthanaram.title: Wat Chaiwatthanaram: Riverside Khmer-Style Temple Ruins in Ayutthaya | ThaiLiveNow
wat-chaiwatthanaram.description: Wat Chaiwatthanaram is a temple ruin on the west side of the Chao Phraya River in Ayutthaya. See Khmer-influenced architecture arranged around a large central tower, surrounding towers and galleries.
intro: On the west side of the Chao Phraya River in Ayutthaya, Wat Chaiwatthanaram is a temple ruin where the large central tower and surrounding towers come into view together. Its clear arrangement of towers and galleries makes it a good place to see the influence of Khmer architecture.

Walk along the surrounding towers and galleries and view the central tower from different angles. Up close, take in the brick structure and ornamentation; from farther away, see how the towers overlap. It is a relaxed visit for companions who want to photograph Ayutthaya’s temple architecture.

experiences.title: A temple arranged around a large central tower
paragraphs: A main tower about 35 m tall stands at the centre of a square compound, with four towers around it. A gallery runs along the perimeter, and towers in eight directions surround the compound. Step back to see at a glance how the large central tower and surrounding structures are arranged.

The layout, influenced by Khmer architecture, is also compared with Angkor Wat. The large central tower with smaller towers around it represents Mount Meru, the centre of the Buddhist cosmos. You can take in both the visible arrangement and its religious meaning.

experiences.title: A king’s temple built in memory of his mother
paragraphs: The temple is said to have been built in 1630 by King Prasat Thong in memory of his late mother. It was later used for royal memorial ceremonies. The impressive towers that remain today have this royal commemorative history behind them.

The temple was burned and abandoned during the war of 1767, then restored in later years before becoming the ruins seen today. The Tourism Authority also describes restoration work in 1987. Walk among the surviving towers and galleries to take in the old temple’s layout and architecture.

experiences.title: A riverside view with overlapping towers
paragraphs: The way the towers overlap in a photograph changes with your position. First look closely at the brickwork, then step back to see the outlines of several towers together. Take your time finding a composition that you like if you are travelling with someone who enjoys architectural photography.

At dusk, the outlines of the central tower and surrounding towers overlap in the view. Visiting hours are listed as **08:00–18:00**, so if you plan to arrive around dusk, schedule your visit using both the sunset time and the closing time for that date.

rules.title: Suggested clothing for a temple visit
paragraphs: For all visitors, we recommend wearing clothing that **covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a good choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

faq: What do the towers around the central prang represent?

Four towers, a surrounding gallery and eight directional towers are arranged around the central prang, which is about 35 metres high. The layout reflects Khmer architectural influence, and the large central tower represents Mount Meru, the centre of the Buddhist universe.
Can I visit the grounds at sunset?

Visiting hours are listed as 08:00–18:00. If you want to see the sunset, check whether that day’s sunset is before 18:00 and plan your visit accordingly. This information does not guarantee night opening or illuminated viewing.

wat-ratchaburana-ayutthaya.name: Wat Ratchaburana
wat-ratchaburana-ayutthaya.thai: วัดราชบูรณะ พระนครศรีอยุธยา
wat-ratchaburana-ayutthaya.type: Temple ruins with a prang in Ayutthaya
wat-ratchaburana-ayutthaya.title: Wat Ratchaburana Ayutthaya: Prang, Temple Ruins and Royal Artifacts | ThaiLiveNow
wat-ratchaburana-ayutthaya.description: Wat Ratchaburana in Ayutthaya is a temple ruin north of Wat Mahathat. Its large prang surrounded by galleries and the remains of halls offer a look at the layout of an early Ayutthaya temple.
intro: At Wat Ratchaburana in Ayutthaya, see a large prang surrounded by galleries and the remains of halls. North of Wat Mahathat, the site preserves the story of a temple built after a royal succession struggle and gold artifacts found inside its tower.

Explore the remaining halls and large tower at the ruins, then visit Chao Sam Phraya National Museum separately to see the excavated objects. If you are interested in both architecture and royal craftsmanship, set aside time for both places. This Ayutthaya site, distinct from the Bangkok temple of the same name, offers a look at the scale of an old royal temple and the artifacts once kept inside it.

experiences.title: A royal temple built in memory of two elder brothers
paragraphs: The dynastic chronicles say that King Borommarachathirat II had this temple built in 1424 on the cremation site of his two elder brothers. After the brothers died together in a fight over the throne while riding elephants, their younger brother became king and established a place to honour them.

experiences.title: The prang and hall foundations on an east–west axis
paragraphs: A gallery surrounds the main prang. The wihan is to the east and the ubosot to the west behind it, arranged along the same axis. The direction of the surviving floors and walls helps you read how the central tower and ceremonial spaces connected.

The Fine Arts Department explains that early Ayutthaya murals influenced by Chinese art remain in a chamber within the tower. The paintings depict past Buddhas, reflecting cultural exchange in royal temple art. **The areas actually open to visitors inside the tower depend on on-site access controls.**

experiences.title: Royal gold objects excavated after looting
paragraphs: After looting in 1956, the Fine Arts Department excavated the tower chamber and found valuable objects, including royal gold artifacts and several Buddha images. These excavated objects are kept at Chao Sam Phraya National Museum.

At the ruins, see the tower and temple grounds where objects were enshrined; at the museum, explore the royal gold pieces and Buddha images found there. The excavated objects are not all exhibited inside the tower, so allow separate time and travel for a museum visit if you want to see the craftsmanship.

rules.title: Suggested clothing for a temple visit
paragraphs: For all visitors, we recommend wearing clothing that **covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a good choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

faq: Why was Wat Ratchaburana in Ayutthaya built?

According to the royal chronicles, King Borommarachathirat II ordered the temple to be built over the cremation site of his two elder brothers, who died while contesting the throne in 1424. This story helps explain the central prang’s role as a royal memorial site.
Where can I see the gold objects found in the prang?

Gold royal objects and Buddha images excavated after a 1956 looting are kept at Chao Sam Phraya National Museum. At the archaeological site, you can see the prang and the remains of the halls; the excavated objects are displayed separately at the museum.

wat-lokayasutharam.name: Wat Lokayasutharam
wat-lokayasutharam.thai: วัดโลกยสุธาราม
wat-lokayasutharam.type: Outdoor reclining Buddha ruins in Ayutthaya
wat-lokayasutharam.title: Wat Lokayasutharam: Outdoor Reclining Buddha in Ayutthaya | ThaiLiveNow
wat-lokayasutharam.description: Wat Lokayasutharam is a ruin in Ayutthaya where you can see a large reclining Buddha outdoors. Unlike the indoor reclining Buddha at Bangkok’s Wat Pho, the sky and surrounding grounds remain in view.
intro: At Wat Lokayasutharam, a large reclining Buddha lies beneath the open sky, without a hall roof. This Ayutthaya ruin offers a view of the image’s face and long body outdoors, a different setting from the indoor reclining Buddha at Wat Pho in Bangkok.

After looking closely at the Buddha’s expression and taking photos, walk around the remains of the old temple. Foundations of large buildings, galleries and a prang remain and give you a sense of the temple that once enshrined the image. As this is an outdoor visit, prepare for sun or rain so you can explore the reclining Buddha and ruins at a relaxed pace.

experiences.title: A 28-metre Reclining Buddha in an open field
paragraphs: A Reclining Buddha about 28 metres long and 5 metres high lies in a broad open area in western Ayutthaya. The image is made of brick covered in plaster; note the lotus-shaped support beneath its head and its long outstretched body. Unlike the indoor Reclining Buddha at Wat Pho in Bangkok, this one can be viewed outdoors in its entirety.

The Tourism Authority describes this image as depicting the Buddha entering nirvana at the age of 80. Look at the face from nearby, then step back to follow the outline all the way to the feet. This helps you take in both the reclining pose and the remains of the old temple grounds.

experiences.title: Remains of the old temple around the Reclining Buddha
paragraphs: This place is also known as Wat Phranorn, or the Temple of the Reclining Buddha. The provincial government says the Ayutthaya chronicles mention King Borommakot’s route here to pay respect to the Reclining Buddha. It was an important temple site near the former royal palace and Wat Phra Si Sanphet.

The grounds also contain traces of large buildings and galleries, as well as the main tower, or prang. After seeing the Reclining Buddha, follow the foundations and the direction in which the galleries once ran. They show that what may now look like an open space was once a large temple complex with several buildings.

experiences.title: Distinguishing the restored Buddha image from the ancient ruins
paragraphs: The Reclining Buddha you see today was restored in 1956. Its present surface is not unchanged from when the old Ayutthaya temple was first built, so consider the restoration date of the image separately from the history of the temple remains around it.

The Tourism Authority notes that no hall roof or intact building remains around the Reclining Buddha. This is an archaeological site where you view the whole image outdoors rather than entering an indoor hall. If it is sunny or raining, plan for the time you will spend outside.

rules.title: Suggested clothing for a temple visit
paragraphs: For all visitors, we recommend wearing clothing that **covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a good choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

faq: How is it different from the Reclining Buddha at Wat Pho?

The Reclining Buddha at Wat Pho in Bangkok is inside a hall, while the one at Wat Lokayasutharam in Ayutthaya lies in an open-air archaeological site without a roof. Here, you can see the whole image, open sky behind it and the remains of the old temple around it.
Is this the Reclining Buddha’s original Ayutthaya-period form?

The Reclining Buddha visible today was restored in 1956. Traces of large buildings, galleries and a prang also remain at the old temple site, so you can see the restored image alongside the locations of the ancient architecture.

wat-yai-chai-mongkhon.name: Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon
wat-yai-chai-mongkhon.thai: วัดใหญ่ชัยมงคล
wat-yai-chai-mongkhon.type: Ayutthaya temple with a large chedi and Buddha images
wat-yai-chai-mongkhon.title: Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon: Large Chedi and Buddha Images in Ayutthaya | ThaiLiveNow
wat-yai-chai-mongkhon.description: Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon is a temple in Ayutthaya with a large chedi and Buddha images around the grounds. Unlike sites where only brick ruins remain, worship still takes place here alongside the historic architecture.
intro: At Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon, the large bell-shaped chedi can be seen from a distance. Up close, this Ayutthaya temple has a tall square base, small towers at its four corners and a Reclining Buddha near the entrance.

The temple began in 1357 as a place of practice for monks who had studied in Sri Lanka. The large chedi is known as a memorial to King Naresuan’s victory in 1592. Today, visitors exploring the ruins and worshippers share the same temple grounds.

experiences.title: A temple for practice founded in 1357
paragraphs: The temple is described as having been founded in 1357 by King U Thong, who established Ayutthaya. It is said to have served as a place for meditation by monks who studied in Sri Lanka. It is also known by the name Wat Phra Chao Phaya Thai.

It is interesting to know that monks practised here before the current large chedi was built. As you look around the tower and surrounding halls, you can reflect on the temple’s long history alongside the former capital.

experiences.title: A victory chedi and the Reclining Buddha at the entrance
paragraphs: The tall bell-shaped chedi is said to have been built in 1592 to commemorate King Naresuan’s victory over the Burmese. The story of the king’s elephant-back duel is associated with this tower, but the temple itself dates back to 1357. The grounds bring together an early temple for practice and a later royal victory memorial.

The Tourism Authority says the large chedi stands on a tall square base, with a small tower at each corner. There is also a large Reclining Buddha at the entrance. First take in the main tower from a distance, then look separately at the entrance Buddha and the images around the base; there is more to see than the tall tower alone.

experiences.title: A temple where people still come to pray
paragraphs: Visitors viewing the old architecture and worshippers come together on the temple grounds. Follow on-site instructions about shoes and movement through the religious areas. Look around quietly and give way to anyone praying in front of an image.

Use only the chedi stairs and interior areas **open on the day of your visit.** Even if you cannot climb to the top, you can view the whole tower from outside and look at the surrounding Buddha images. Follow the on-site access guidance and explore at a comfortable pace.

rules.title: Suggested clothing for a temple visit
paragraphs: For all visitors, we recommend wearing clothing that **covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a good choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

faq: Was there a temple here before the large chedi was built?

Yes. The temple is described as having begun in 1357 as a place of practice for monks who had studied in Sri Lanka. The large victory chedi was built much later, in 1592, to commemorate King Naresuan’s victory.
What can I see if I cannot climb the chedi stairs?

From outside, you can view the large bell-shaped chedi and the smaller towers at its four corners, then see the Reclining Buddha near the entrance and the images around the base. Use only the stairs and interior sections open on the day of your visit.

wat-phanan-choeng.name: Wat Phanan Choeng
wat-phanan-choeng.thai: วัดพนัญเชิง
wat-phanan-choeng.type: Ayutthaya temple housing a large golden seated Buddha
wat-phanan-choeng.title: Wat Phanan Choeng: Luang Pho To Buddha and Temple Visit | ThaiLiveNow
wat-phanan-choeng.description: Wat Phanan Choeng is an Ayutthaya temple housing a large golden seated Buddha about 19 m tall. Unlike visits to ruined brick temple grounds, the focus here is the hall enshrining the image.
intro: Enter the hall at Wat Phanan Choeng and a large golden seated Buddha, about 19 m tall, fills the space. The temple predates Ayutthaya’s time as a capital, and you can see Chinese-influenced decoration as well as worship that continues today.

Wat Phanan Choeng adds a living place of worship to a tour of Ayutthaya’s old ruins. Alongside the large Buddha known as Luang Pho To, there are other Buddha images and a hall housing Guanyin. After seeing the large image, take time to explore the different worship spaces inside and around the halls.

experiences.title: The large seated Buddha known as Luang Pho To and Sam Po Kong
paragraphs: The golden seated Buddha, about 19 m tall, is called Phra Phuttha Trairattana Nayok, or Luang Pho To. Among Chinese devotees, it is also known as Sam Po Kong. The large image seen from inside the hall and the Chinese-influenced decoration around it are striking together.

An offering ceremony, in which devotees drape cloth over the Buddha image, is another feature of the temple. If you see the ceremony taking place, quietly move aside from the route used by worshippers. It is not a scheduled performance for tourists, so do not plan your visit on the assumption that you will always see it.

experiences.title: A temple that predates Ayutthaya’s time as a capital
paragraphs: Wat Phanan Choeng was built in 1324, before Ayutthaya became the capital. The area also has a long history of Chinese residents. At a temple visited by both Thai and Chinese devotees, you can see Chinese-influenced decoration and worship traditions too.

experiences.title: Other Buddha images and worship spaces in the main hall
paragraphs: The main hall enshrines other Buddha images as well as the large seated one, including gold images, plaster-covered images and a copper-alloy image. After admiring the golden Buddha, look at the other images in turn. You can see statues made from different materials together.

There is also a shrine to Soi Dok Mak and a shrine to Guanyin on the grounds. Visitors interested in religious art can see several Buddhist and Chinese devotional figures in one temple. Please explore quietly without blocking people praying in the halls.

rules.title: Suggested clothing for a temple visit
paragraphs: For all visitors, we recommend wearing clothing that **covers the shoulders and knees**. A sleeved top with long trousers or a skirt that covers the knees is a good choice. Please dress modestly rather than wearing a sleeveless top or short bottoms.

faq: Was this temple built after Ayutthaya became the capital?
No. Wat Phanan Choeng was founded in 1324, before Ayutthaya became the capital. Worship still takes place in front of the large seated Buddha known as Luang Pho To.
Are Luang Pho To and Sam Pao Kong different Buddha images?

They are two names for the same golden seated Buddha, about 19 metres high. Luang Pho To is the name used by Thai worshippers, while Sam Pao Kong is used by Chinese worshippers. There is also a shrine to Guanyin on the temple grounds.
